# Thread: Research Pipeline

**Model, and why it is recorded here.** Added 2026-09-04 so the choice is
explicit rather than drifting. **The honest state of the evidence: there is
none yet supporting differentiation.** Every thread on 2026-09-04 caught a
subtle defect in its own work that a weaker model plausibly misses, and the
capacity actually burned that night was message VOLUME, not model strength.
**A downgrade recorded as a saving without a measurement would be this desk's
"constant dressed as a measurement".** What would settle it: run a thread's
next self-contained task at a smaller model and compare what it catches.

**Model: Opus 5.** On 2026-09-04 it caught that its own new allowlist refuses silently — the same failure mode as the defect it replaced — and designed a split-before-parse so a shares-outstanding figure is unreachable by construction rather than merely unmatched.

**Owns what the desk knows and what it pays to know it.** Evidence collection,
source resolution, the interpreter, dossier quality, and the OpenAI bill.

Last worked: **2026-08-27**. See **LIVE STATE** below before anything else.

## Why this is its own thread

Every one of these arrived looking like a production incident and was actually a
research-pipeline decision about cost:

| Date | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-08-18 | 403 research jobs in a day, >12M input tokens — duplicate recovery and qualification work |
| 2026-08-19 | Interpreter dead on an empty OpenAI balance; diagnosis cost a live API probe |
| 2026-08-20 | 6.68M input tokens drained the balance again |
| 2026-08-21 | Whole Top 12 dark from 04:00–08:00 ET; 58 failed jobs across 21 tickers, 112 model calls, 0 tokens |

Ops kept absorbing these. The fix is always in `lib/research/`.

## Scope

- `lib/research/` — queue, retry policy, provider errors, interpreter
- Source resolution and catalyst collection; the resolver-first path and the
  urgent first-qualification path for a newly qualifying Top-12 name
- Dossier grading and honesty: `UNKNOWN` and `PARTIAL` are real verdicts, not
  failures
- Model selection and token budget

Background on how the pipeline was built and why:
[../RESEARCH-MILESTONE-PLAN.md](../RESEARCH-MILESTONE-PLAN.md).

## Not this thread

- Deploying → [ops.md](ops.md)
- How dossiers are *presented* → [design.md](design.md)
- **The market archive and the market-structure question** →
  [rnd.md](rnd.md). Split out 2026-08-23: this thread generates incidents, and a
  thread owning both an incident stream and an open research question will only
  ever work on the incidents. This thread's job is that the pipeline produces
  honest catalyst grades at a defensible cost. What those grades *mean* is R&D.

in **which option it picks**.

  **WHY NOT IN-RANGE: neither field can be recomputed for an arbitrary range.** `rankChange` needs a PREVIOUS ranking in that same range, and previous ranks exist only for the qualify band — holding one per viewer range is unbounded. `deadAtRank` is a historical fact about a name that is gone; producing it for a new range needs a re-rank of a past moment against a membership that was never recorded. **Mixing them is worse than either: an in-range rank minus a global previous rank is a delta between two different lists.**
  **WHY NOT LABEL IT: this desk's usual cure is "convert AND label", and here conversion is impossible, so labelling would put a SECOND denominator on a row that §2 has just given one** — *"top 25 of 312"* beside *"held rank 7 of \$1–\$20"*. **Two frames on one row is the defect the caption rule exists to remove.**
  **WHY SERVER-SIDE: omission at the server makes the field ABSENT, so there is no render path that can forget the rule.** *A component told not to print something is a rule; a field that is not there is a constraint.*
  **⚠️ AND THE CONDITION IS "THE REQUESTED RANGE ≠ THE BAND THE ORDINALS WERE COMPUTED IN", NOT "≠ THE DEFAULT".** The stored ordinals are computed in the QUALIFY band. ~~Today the default range and the qualify band coincide at `\$1–\$20`, so the two conditions agree~~ **CORRECTED 2026-09-28: they do NOT coincide — production's qualify band is `\$0.25–\$20` (`DISCOVERY_PRICE_MIN=0.25`, no MAX line), his board default is `\$1–\$20`, so the default range is itself re-ranked (`af15a13`). Neither is driven by TIME SINCE THE LAST LOOK when the answer was a negative** — and a catalyst being indexed on a wire is neither. **There is no path by which the passage of time alone makes the desk ask again about a name it has already said no about.**

  **WHAT IT DOES TO THE 27 catalyst-less verdicts: AIFF's was SOUND** — fetch ran, feed reachable, nothing recent in it — **and a public catalyst existed the whole time. The instrument was honest and the answer was wrong**, so every other verdict in that set inherits the same doubt. That is not a collector defect; it is the ask-once design showing through a working collector.
  **Q1, DELIBERATELY UNANSWERED:** whether `fireflyneuro.com/rss` carries wire releases at all is a fact about that feed, settled by fetching it **from the box with the production user-agent** — not from a seat whose request would measure itself rather than the desk. If the 09-25 item is absent, the issuer-feed route cannot see wire-only releases by construction, which is a blind spot of a different order from latency.

- **⚠️ `eventTimestamp` IS THE `freshness` DEFECT'S TWIN AND IT IS STILL LIVE. Established in code 2026-09-25, NOT yet sized.** The four-day thread took `freshness` away from the model because `schema.ts` declared the enum with no description and the prompt never defined it. **The arithmetic that replaced it reads `catalyst.eventTimestamp` — and that is a model output against `schema.ts:90` `eventTimestamp: nullableString`, declared with NO description, about ten lines from the comment explaining why `freshness` was removed for exactly that.** `SYSTEM_PROMPT_A` (`openaiInterpreter.ts:70`) never mentions it: searched for `eventTimestamp`, "newest", "most recent", "latest", "select the", "choose the" — nothing. The model is handed a bundle and never told which source's time to put there.
  **And nothing validates it.** `guardrails.ts:265` `checkIds` confirms the cited source ids EXIST in the bundle; `guardrails.ts:338` recomputes `freshness` FROM the timestamp. **No check ever compares `eventTimestamp` to the `published_at` of any source the catalyst cites** — the stamp is not constrained even to its own evidence. So the band is computed honestly from a number nobody constrains.
  **The operational consequence, settled for Ops 2026-09-25 before the `0a17601` ship:** a ticker's newest ACTIVE SOURCE being in band does NOT imply its SELECTED CATALYST is. Those are different quantities, and `max(published_at)` across active sources is an upper bound on candidates rather than a count of movers.
  **NOT sized, and no mechanism proposed.** The obvious repair — constrain the stamp to the cited sources' published times — is exactly the shape of thing that needs a count first; see the `20:00:00 ET` trap in the hazards, found the same morning by having the measurement and reading it the wrong way round for a moment.

- **⚠️ THE PRIOR-SESSION-CLOSE FRESH WINDOW: PRODUCER SHIPPED `7a0ad0c`, CONSUMER IS DESIGN'S AND NOT DONE.** `684902f` implements the band; `7a0ad0c` supplies the boundary as **`MarketSnapshot.catalystFreshFrom`**, computed once per snapshot server-side in `getMarketSnapshot`, null on both degraded snapshots and whenever the answer would be a guess. **Nothing on his board changes until Design passes it as the third argument** at `lib/dashboard/why.ts:239` — four `resolveWhy` call sites, routed to Design through Integration 2026-09-25. Until then **clocked after-hours releases still band RECENT** (6 rows in the 2026-08-23 snapshot), which is his date-only rule and is safe.
  **Two decisions inside `7a0ad0c` that went beyond the spec, both asserted in `tests/research/catalystFreshFrom.test.ts`:** it takes the **prior session's OWN close** rather than `afterHoursStartUtc`'s 16:00 default, which is three hours late the day after an early close; and the producer **refuses a stale calendar** rather than leaning on `resolveCatalystFreshness`'s five-day guard — and the test is that **the calendar still covers the date asked about**, not the size of the gap to the previous session, because an unscheduled closure produces the same gap with a current calendar and there the wide window is CORRECT. `calendarDays` is now exported from `lib/desk/checkpointDates.ts` rather than the calendar being parsed a third time.
  **`catalystFreshFrom` ABSENT AS A KEY AND PRESENT-AND-NULL ARE DIFFERENT DIAGNOSES, and Design established that production currently has NO KEY** (2026-09-25), so "`7a0ad0c` is not live" is measured rather than assumed. After it ships the key is ALWAYS present — all three return sites in `getMarketSnapshot` set it — so **a null after the ship means the store was read and the boundary was refused** (no trading date, no calendar, or a calendar that no longer covers the date), which is a different thing to chase than a missing key.
  **Size: 6 of 325 analyses, RE-MEASURED by this seat 2026-09-25 rather than inherited.** On `data/market-prod-2026-08-23.db`, through the shipped `resolveCatalystFreshness` rather than a second implementation of the band: 260 of 325 carry an event timestamp, **59 of those 260 carry a clock (201 bare, 77%)**, and **6 change band — every one of them RECENT → FRESH**, all clocked releases between 16:30 and 20:00 ET (XOS x2, TRUG, AIXC, PURR, ABUS). **THAT NUMBER IS DENOMINATED IN STORED ANALYSES AND MUST NOT BE CARRIED TO A DEPLOY CHECK.** The board is a different population: Design measured the live Discovery board at 09:15 ET on 2026-09-25 and found **12 rows with exactly ONE candidate** (`INLF`, a 17:18 ET catalyst that must turn green), six controls that must not move and one bare date that cannot. Both numbers are right and they answer different questions — 6 is the reach across everything stored, 1 is what a verifier should expect to see change. **An expected value borrowed from another population fires at VERIFICATION time, where a false negative is filed as a regression.**

- **Phase C, filing-derived float — THE CONTAINMENT HALF ALREADY SHIPPED, AND IT IS NOT `assessFloat`.** *Corrected 2026-09-25; the hand-off prompt and the line this replaces both said "`assessFloat` already IS the containment test", which is true of that function and wrong about the board.* **`assessFloat` (`float.ts:326`) has never had a production caller** — not at HEAD and not anywhere in history (`git log -S`); it is exported, carries 30-odd assertions in `tests/research/float.test.ts`, and has only ever been called by its own tests. What the board actually runs is **`assessFloatAgainstFiled`** (`float.ts:606`, wired at `lib/dashboard/merge.ts:276`), shipped `7cc5076` on 2026-09-22 as **his four states** — `REFUTED` / `CONSISTENT` / `CONSISTENT_STALE` / `CANNOT_VERIFY`. Its own docstring says the two must not be collapsed: `assessFloat` judges on the RESEARCH side and refuses what it cannot stand behind; the shipped one judges a BORROWED vendor float for the TRADER, where "I cannot check this" is one of the answers he asked for.

It is a box question for Ops. **The read is specced and committed — `integration.md`, `0d60b33` — including the condition that it must return the THREE INPUT COUNTS (Sheet `float.value`, dossier `supplyPair.sharesOutstanding`, basis factor) alongside the verdict counts, because the verdict fails closed on each independently and a 100% `CANNOT_VERIFY` histogram has at least four explanations.** Pointer rather than a copy; the spec lives in one place. **A is a prerequisite, not an option:** build-vs-drop does not go to him until the number exists.
  What that snapshot CAN say, measured 2026-09-25 on its own field names (`structure.sharesOutstanding`, the pre-`supplyPair` shape — **the first pass read `supplyPair` and returned 0 for every row, which was the instrument and not the world**): 125 of 325 analyses carry a share count, 124 of those carry a date, and only 7 carry a dossier float at all — because the float on the board comes from the Sheet, not the dossier.

That predates his 2026-09-19 ruling and is superseded by the standing constraint.*
- **31 personal-scoped justifications in this file.** Integration counted 86 across nine charters. **Fix as each finding is touched**; a bulk rewrite of reasons is how a wrong reason gets a confident new sentence.

### STANDING CONSTRAINTS — things that must NOT be done

- **NO HEAVY READ AGAINST PRODUCTION `market.db` WHILE A DEPLOY UNIT IS RUNNING — ask Ops for the window.** Ops's finding 2026-09-25, `README.md` `20b2499`. `quick_check` is a `PRAGMA quick_check` full integrity scan of a **3.5G** file, already running **388–597s against a 900s follow deadline**, and the false `is live` fires when a unit is still running at that deadline — **measured margin 132s on the day's worst deploy.** A concurrent census scan is exactly what pushes it over. **So a measurement of mine can make the deploy tool announce a cutover of mine that has not happened, and nothing in my query's own result would show it.** This binds the `collector_report` scan for `candidatesReturned/Probed/Fetched`, which starts accumulating next session and is precisely the kind of full scan meant here.
  **⚠️ AND IT LANDS ON THE 10s CAPTURE DESIGN, WHICH IS WHY IT IS HERE AND NOT ONLY IN THE HAZARDS.** `quick_check` scans the WHOLE FILE, so **anything that grows `market.db` lengthens every future deploy's integrity check and eats that 132s margin.** Sized against the population choice, upper bound from the local store: **top-12 at 5-day retention is ~292k rows (~30MB, ~1% growth) — negligible. Top-250 at 20-day is ~15.8M rows (~1.6GB), which would be a 45% increase in the file `quick_check` must scan.** *So the population and retention choice for 10s capture is a DEPLOY-SAFETY decision as well as a storage one, and it would otherwise be discovered by a deploy timing out.*
  **The store's LOCATION is therefore a question for Ops, not this seat.** A separate database file keeps `quick_check` off the 10s buckets entirely and makes the population choice purely a storage question — and the desk already runs `archive.db`, `assessments.db` and `identity.db` beside `market.db`, so the pattern exists. **But a new database file defines, migrates and versions tables, which is Ops's by the `lib/market/` split.** Raised, not decided.
  **The ORDERING half is separate and also binds a measurement: Ops's before-reading moved to AFTER cutover and BEFORE the restart.** A web-tier deploy does not touch `minute_bars`, so nothing was lost by taking it later — **but taking it after the RESTART would have destroyed it, because the restart is the event the reading exists to bracket.** Two boundaries that look interchangeable; only one is.

- **DO NOT PUT DEPLOY TIMING TO HIM FOR A BACKEND-ONLY CHANGE. Integration approves clean enumerations to Ops without returning per-deploy** — standing approval recorded `2026-09-23T03:58Z` in `integration.md`, which **supersedes the earlier today-only grant**. What still goes to him: **spend, auth-model changes, destructive actions, and an unreviewed BOARD-BEHAVIOUR change.** Restarts are not Integration's to relay either — Ops takes that word from him directly. *Verified at the artifact 2026-09-25 rather than taken from the relay, and it held.* **This seat spent his attention on a call he had already delegated, by not looking for the grant.** The hand-off prompt warns that a superseded grant reads exactly like a live one; **the inverse costs too, and it is the cheaper mistake to make twice** — a live standing grant reads exactly like no grant if nobody opens the file.

- **Never fetch `stockanalysis.com` from a worker, an API route or a scheduled job.** Their terms bar automated access AND bar using the data in a competing product. His ruling 2026-09-19: the vendor float stays on **his desktop ChatGPT task**, not the API. Volume is ~150/day, small enough that automating it will keep looking like an easy win.
- **The cycle frame is RULED WHOLE: 04:00–20:00 ET.** After-hours 2026-09-17; premarket **2026-09-22T22:35Z, his words "premarket in"**, recorded verbatim by Integration at `3dc0c41`. That ruling was recorded FALSE three times first (`f0048eb`, `3308fb1`, `bb2901d`) off a peer's sentence rather than his own — check the record, not a relay.
- **`BACKSIDE_RETRACEMENT = 0.5` and `SUPERRUNNER_ADVANCE = 2.0` are RE-DERIVED and the FRAME WARNINGS are gone** (2026-09-23). Both held. Backside: the recovery cliff is at 0.5 in both frames and the all-sessions frame makes it *sharper* — P(new high afterwards) falls 40%→10% across it, against 24%→11% in RTH. Superrunner: the frame moves the median (71%→90%) but not the tail (90th 307%→305%), and at n=68 the 90th's 95% interval [218%, 441%] contains 200%, so the sample cannot site it more finely. **They may now be cited as measured, with their window: 75 symbols, 62 sessions, 2026-05-20..08-18.**
- **Both frames must be built from the ONE hourly file**, never paired with `daily_bars`. The file was fetched 2026-09-17 and the daily rows in August; 19 of 75 symbols had corporate actions in-window, and that cross-vintage pairing produced an arithmetically impossible row (an all-sessions high *below* the RTH high) before it was abandoned.

### HAZARDS A FRESH SESSION MUST KNOW

- **⚠️ QUOTING HIM VERBATIM CARRIES THE CLAUSES NEXT TO IT, WHICH MAY BE ADDRESSED TO ANOTHER SEAT. New failure mode, 2026-09-25, and it is the MIRROR of the rule that produced it.** This desk quotes his own words rather than paraphrasing precisely so a relay cannot drift. **That same fidelity delivered this seat an instruction it was never given:** Integration quoted *"0-50 confirmed. handoff, write the prompt, engage hygiene protocol"* to verify the band ruling — **the first clause was the verification; the rest was addressed to OPS in the Ops session**, which acted on it correctly. *And it is MORE convincing than a paraphrase, because it is genuinely his voice.*
  **The fix is one line of discipline: quote the clause, and NAME THE SEAT the rest was addressed to.**
  **What made it catchable was saying WHICH evidence was acted on.** This seat wrote out its three independent signals instead of writing *"on his instruction"* — and Integration checked because the reasoning was visible. **A decision justified by a relay alone gives nobody a reason to look.**

- **⚠️ A TEST-FILE COUNT IS A SHORT-COLLECTION SIGNAL ONLY AGAINST THE COUNT FOR *THAT TREE*. This seat got it wrong on 2026-09-25 and told Ops to distrust a working gate.** A real short collection happened that day — a run reported 3 failed files and 8 errors while collecting **2,339 tests where ~2,470 were expected**, which is memory pressure wearing the appearance of a code defect. **But the NEXT count I challenged was sound.** Ops's gate reported **157 files** at `79cc4d1`; I compared it to main's 164–166 and called it short. Counted at the trees themselves:

| sha | test files |
| --- | ---: |
| `3dc14e2` (production) | 156 |
| `79cc4d1` (production + 2 picks) | **157** |
| `c00992e` (+ `8942a94`) | 157 |
| `8942a94` (main) | 165 |
| `d734d6f` (main) | 166 |

  **A cherry-pick branch carries eight fewer test files than main — my own work among them — so 157 was a smaller TREE, not a short collection.** I compared a number denominated in one population against one denominated in another, **which is the exact count-frame error I had corrected three times that day**, and I did it while accusing someone else's instrument. *Telling a peer to distrust a working gate is the more expensive direction: it costs a re-run and it teaches doubt about a correct result.*
  **THE PRACTICE, cheap and now standard: PREDICT THE COUNT BEFORE THE GATE.** `git ls-tree -r --name-only <base> | grep -cE '\.(test|spec)\.(ts|tsx)$'`, then add the test files the pick introduces. `d734d6f` adds exactly one, so its gate onto `c00992e` must report **158**. **A number ruling out short collection beats an argument about one.**

- **⚠️ `collector_report` ROWS FROM 2026-08-18 UNTIL `d19355c` DEPLOYS CARRY `companySourceDetail: 'not attempted'` ON SUCCESSFUL FETCHES, AND NO FETCH WITNESS AT ALL.** The affected window opens at `8c94390` / `8f212fe`, both 2026-08-18. **Production is `0a17601`, whose `collector.ts` is `ea2d1c9`, so the window is still open.** `d19355c` repairs the FUTURE and cannot repair the census: anyone re-partitioning stored rows on that field gets the wrong answer again, and the comment explaining why is not in the release they are reading.
  **What that field actually means: RESOLUTION, not the fetch.** `collector.ts:189` declares it *"what issuer-source resolution did, or why it was not offered a turn"*, and resolution is gated on `!usableCompanySourceBefore` — so `'not attempted'` is CORRECT and healthy for any ticker that already has a usable url on file. **It never meant the desk did not look.** A production census of 173 jobs read it the other way on 2026-09-25 and concluded the collector returns "no catalyst" without looking; R&D halted a count on that. Both were withdrawn.
  **`AIFF` on 2026-09-25 is inside the window and is NOT answerable from the table**, now or later: qualified 07:48:00.711, job 07:48:01.268–07:48:31.977, `sourcesAdded 0`, fingerprint identical to its 09-18 job — which is equally what a successful fetch of an unchanged feed produces, since `research_sources` inserts are `INSERT OR IGNORE`. **Leave it open rather than concluding it.**
  **After `d19355c` deploys, `companyFetchDetail` and `networkRequests` are both persisted**, so fetched-and-empty is distinguishable from never-fetched from the table rather than from an argument about control flow that three seats re-derived in one afternoon.
  **THE REGISTER STATUS IS "WE WILL KNOW ONCE THIS SHIPS", NOT "WE CANNOT KNOW" — they are different claims and only the second is permanent.** The window is dated and closes on deploy; rows written after it carry the answer. **Only the rows already written, `AIFF`'s among them, are permanently unanswerable.** A retrospective read cannot substitute for the forward one and should not be offered as one.
  **And the string carries the ITEM COUNT rather than a boolean, which separates a channel nobody had named when it was written:** a read failure routes to `COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE`, but **a clean parse yielding nothing falls through to `NO_RECENT_SOURCE_LOCATED` and is indistinguishable from a true negative.** `read 40 items` versus `read 0 items` tells "the feed had plenty, none recent" from "the parser got nothing out of it". *R&D reached that question independently and it is answered from the table — by luck of the shape chosen, not by foresight.*

- **`minute_bars` IS A PARTIAL ARCHIVE BY DESIGN, AND THREE DIFFERENT CAUSES COLLAPSE INTO THE SAME ZERO ROWS.** Established in code 2026-09-25 after a coaching export found three symbol-dates he TRADED with no bars at all (`GSUN` 09-16 and `SDST` 09-17, zero rows on any date; `SNYR` captured 09-10 and 09-11 only). **`worker/runtime.ts:1485` filters the live-stream write to tracked symbols** — *"whole-market bar traffic is not a tick warehouse"* — so a name inside the price band that never becomes tracked is **subscribed, received, ranked, and deliberately not retained.**
  **⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-26: THAT IS THE RIGHT MECHANISM AND THE WRONG ONE FOR THOSE THREE NAMES.** `GSUN` 0.232, `SDST` 0.115 and `SNYR` 0.0905 are **below every floor this desk has run** (0.25 in production, 1 as the code default at `config.ts:71`). **`engine.ts:985-993`: a symbol with no runtime is admitted only if its bar close is `inPriceRange`, so a sub-floor name never gets a runtime at all — never tracked, never ranked, never persisted.** *The retention filter fires second and only for names that got that far.* **So "ranked" was wrong: the desk did not decline to keep their bars, it never looked at them.** That is a stronger fact than the one it replaces and it was found by reading the admission branch rather than the retention one.
  **The board does NOT miss movers by this mechanism, and the ordering is the proof:** `runtime.ts:1266-1272` calls `this.engine.ingest(observation)` **unconditionally, BEFORE** queuing the bar for persistence. Every whole-market bar reaches the engine, so discovery ranks over the entire market; only the archive is filtered. Bars are wildcard-subscribed at `stream.ts:298`; the degraded-universe fallback logs itself at `stream.ts:311` and is distinguishable from the LOG but not from the store.
  **What IS true and is the finding: never tracked, tracked and silent, and never subscribed are ONE observation in `minute_bars` — zero rows.** `SNYR` is the informative case and needs no ticker mismatch to explain: tracking is per-date and follows the board, so it ranked twice and not the third time.
  **The consequence lands on retrospective work, not on the desk:** the archive is partial in exactly the population coaching cares about — names he traded that never ranked. Excluding them explicitly and stating the reduced n is the right handling, not a workaround.
  **The reusable half, and this desk hit both sides of it in one day:** `catalystFreshFrom` ABSENT-as-a-key versus PRESENT-and-null is distinguishable, and that is what let Design MEASURE "`7a0ad0c` is not live" instead of assuming it. Here three causes share one zero. **Whether a store can tell its own failure modes apart is a question to ask BEFORE running a measurement over it, not after the result comes back interesting.**

- **⚠️ DO NOT "FIX" THE ET WALL-CLOCK TIMESTAMPS INTO CLOCK PRECISION. MEASURED 2026-09-25, AND IT IS A TRAP THAT LOOKS LIKE A BUG.** Three shapes are live in the catalyst timestamp column today — `2026-09-24T21:18:05.000Z`, `2026-09-25T04:41:22-04:00`, and `2026-09-25T08:30:32 ET`. The third gets **DATE** precision, so it can never reach FRESH through the prior-close boundary: **the same event written three ways bands two ways**, and after `catalystFreshFrom` is wired that shows on the board as an amber row beside two green ones for a reason invisible on it. That reads exactly like a defect in the new feature.
  **It is not, and the count says why. 33 of 260 stored timestamps carry the ` ET` shape — and 31 of those 33 are EXACTLY `20:00:00 ET`,** the end of the after-hours session. That is a FILL VALUE, not an observed release time. Parsing them as clocks would promote **7 analyses RECENT → FRESH out of a storage convention** — the same defect `3570114` fixed when bare dates were rendering as `16h`, arriving by a new route. The remaining two (`05:19:28`, `17:00:00`) are the only ones that look observed.
  **THE NUMBER THAT WILL MAKE THE WRONG FIX LOOK OVERDUE, and it is why the instruction above is load-bearing rather than a footnote.** Ops's census of the CURRENT dossiers, 2026-09-25 — **a different and larger population than the 33 of 260 above**, which is `research_analysis_versions` on a month-old snapshot:

| shape | count | reaches FRESH? |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `Z` (CLOCK) | 498 | yes |
| numeric offset (CLOCK) | 32 | yes |
| ` ET` (DATE) | 74 | **never** |
| other, incl. bare dates | 270 | **never** |
| **total with a catalyst timestamp** | **874** | |

  **344 of 874 — over a third — can never reach FRESH by construction.** It fails in the safe direction, but 344 is exactly the size of number that makes someone read it as under-reporting and reach for `etWallClockToUtc`, which promotes the 31 `20:00:00 ET` fill values. *Design's direction note, which sharpens this: the fill-value error can ONLY ever promote, never demote — so it could never appear as a wrong band, only as too many greens. **A defect with no failing appearance is one nobody reports.*** **The concrete row to point at, named by Ops: `YMAT`, `2026-09-23T20:00:00 ET` — a live production instance of the fill value, not a hypothetical.**

  **⚠️ AND THAT CENSUS PUTS A QUESTION MARK OVER THE "77%" THIS DESK QUOTES IN SIX PLACES** — `time.ts:323`, `time.ts:386`, `guardrails.ts:334`, `why.ts:68`, `why.ts:246`, and the `d16dd14` row above, where it is **the stated reason his rule is calendar days rather than hours** (`d16dd14` reads *"Freshness is his calendar bands now, and `Date.parse` cannot compute them"*, so it is load-bearing for the ruling rather than merely quoted near it). **There was a SIXTH code site and I wrote it this morning:** `lib/market/types.ts:767`, the doc comment on `catalystFreshFrom` in `7a0ad0c`. I copied the figure into new code without its denominator and then flagged the same figure four hours later. Found by Integration checking my list rather than recording it. **Corrected at `f06b89b`** — it now states 344 of 874 current dossiers, with its population named and the discrepancy pointed at this hazard. That 77% is denominated in the 08-23 snapshot's 260 timestamps. Ops's current-dossier census has `Z` alone at 57% where that snapshot had 18%. **THE TWO ARE DIFFERENT POPULATIONS and I have NOT measured the current one, so nothing here is a claim that 77% is wrong** — it is a claim that the figure is old, denominated somewhere else, and load-bearing. **What would settle it: the same shape census over the population the 77% actually refers to.** Do not quote 77% again without its denominator, and do not reopen his day-band ruling on a relayed number — if clock coverage really has moved that far, he ruled on a premise that has changed and he is owed the measurement, not the inference.

  **So the DATE treatment is right, and for a stronger reason than the one recorded below:** not merely that the offset is unstated, but that 94% of these values state a time nobody published. `etWallClockToUtc` (`lib/market/session.ts`) exists and would convert them correctly, which is exactly what makes this worth writing down — the fix is easy, available, and wrong.

- **`Date.parse` ON AN `eventTimestamp` AGES IT BY A DAY.** **200 of the 260 stored values are bare dates** like `2026-08-17`, and `Date.parse` reads those as midnight UTC, which is **20:00 ET the previous day**. Anything computing an age or a band from them skews one day stale. Use `catalystAge` / `eventEtDate` (`lib/research/time.ts`); never `Date.parse`. The stored data also holds ET wall clocks (`2026-08-16 20:00:00 ET`) whose `Date.parse` behaviour is implementation-defined and whose offset is not stated — those get DATE precision, not CLOCK.
- **The EX-99 latency measurement is FORWARD-LOOKING and the existing 878 exhibits can never answer it.** `research_sources` inserts are `INSERT OR IGNORE` and nothing updates `published_at`/`published_precision`, so stored rows are frozen. A fresh snapshot does not help. The measurable population is EX-99 exhibits whose **parent filing row** was inserted after `b1d64b9` — and exhibits inherit from the **stored** parent, which is frozen too. Partition on whether `published_at` carries a clock, not on the precision label.
- **`daily_bars.high` is 09:30–16:00 plus the closing cross.** Premarket excluded 18–0, evening excluded, 0 of 121 discriminating rows premarket-inclusive. **The same bar's VOLUME is not RTH-only** (3 of 2,747 rows, 0.1%) — one bar, two windows, and `bootstrapSession`'s docstring cites the volume property right where the high is also taken.
- **Today is not in the cycle input.** `readDailyBars` defaults to `unfinished: 'EXCLUDE'`, so a name up 270% right now is judged as of yesterday. This is the QCLS mechanism (incident `ops.md:10297`, 2026-09-16) and what `e48a2ca` supplies.
- **`volume_base` / `volume_base_through` were literals** until Ops fixed them; `volume_base_source` now writes the unmutated source. Earliest non-null `volume_base_through` dates the daily-bar roll — **not** first nonzero `volume_base`, which conflates rolled with traded.
- **Calibration data, audited:** `data/vendor/alpaca-1hour-split-2026-05-20-to-2026-08-18.json` (75 symbols, 62 sessions, gitignored). Derive from the **split** file. The `-raw-` file beside it is incomplete for **MSS** — a truncated fetch, 45 dense dates then a partial day then nothing.
- **19 of 75 symbols had corporate actions in-window**, at clean factors up to 200:1. My earlier "89% drift" and "within-symbol basis inconsistency" claims are **both withdrawn** — the filters that produced them were circular.

**`volume_base` IS THE LITERAL `0` ON EVERY ROW.** `worker/runtime.ts:1752-1753`
writes `volume_base: 0` and `volume_base_through: null` as hardcoded literals;
**25,789 of 25,789** rows confirm both. The engine holds the real values and the
writer throws them away, and `volume_base_source` duplicates `volume_source`
byte for byte. **This is what makes Ops's item #1 unmeasurable:**
`cumulativeVolume = volumeBase + minuteSum` (`engine.ts:1405`), so a nonzero
premarket volume proves a rolled bar **or** a name that merely traded while we
streamed -- and premarket movers trade. The one field that would split the sum
is the constant. *A constant is more dangerous than a null: my four premarket
snapshots on 2026-08-18 read 25/25 nonzero and looked like an answer.*

> **AND IT IS WORSE THAN A MISSING VALUE, which is Integration-tmi's addition.**

**BOTH RESIDUES CLOSED, AND THEY WERE MY INSTRUMENT'S RESOLUTION, NOT THE DATA.**
Integration-tmi flagged that I had led with TEST 1's zero while the conclusion
rests on TEST 2, which still carried an unexplained 18.2%. Correct, and the four
rows they asked to see resolved the whole thing.

**THE PREMARKET RESIDUE IS THE 09:30 BOUNDARY.** An hourly bar starting 09:00 ET
**straddles the open**, so its high may fall either side of 09:30 and hourly data
cannot split it. An RTH-only daily bar takes only the post-09:30 part, which
means it must land in the band:

    RTH(10:00-16:00) max   <=   daily.high   <=   straddle(09:00-10:00) max

**37 of 39 residue rows fall exactly in that band.** The other two (BLND 08-17
1.490 vs 1.488; VTRS 07-14 16.43 vs 16.41) match the RTH max **exactly** and miss
the upper bound at the third decimal -- rounding, not anomaly. **39 of 39.**

**THE AFTER-HOURS RESIDUE IS THE CLOSING CROSS** -- all four set their high in the
16:00-17:00 ET hour, three with no 04:00-16:00 trades at all.

⇒ **ONE RULE EXPLAINS BOTH TABLES: `daily_bars.high` is 09:30-16:00 plus the
closing cross.** Premarket-inclusive: **0 of 121**, zero in every population and
every basis treatment I tried.

**AND THE REAL LESSON IS MY OWN INSTABILITY, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE
FINDING.** Across four filter variants the residue read **0% -> 18.2% -> 27.3% ->
5.0% -> 32.2%** on the same data. **A quantity that moves that much under
filter choice is measuring the filter.** Two of those filters were circular in
ways I did not see:

- *Basis-consistency by `daily/hourly_allday` spread* -- **the spread is produced
  by the window effect being tested**, so it selected "symbols that never had an
  extended-session high" and called it a basis property. My "67 of 75 drift in
  basis" claim came from this and **is withdrawn.**
- *Each date's ratio against that symbol's MEDIAN ratio* -- the median is
  dominated by days whose high sits in RTH, so **a day whose high fell outside
  RTH is required to deviate.** The instrument flagged the finding as the anomaly.

**The stored daily series has NO split discontinuity** (largest consecutive close
jump 6.46x on RCON, 3.52x on PFSA -- not the 200x a mixed-vintage table would
show), so `daily_bars` is uniformly adjusted and **the within-symbol basis
inconsistency I reported is also withdrawn.**

**What survived every variant was the DIRECTION: premarket-inclusive never scored
above zero.** A conclusion that holds across four differently-broken filters is
worth more than a residue rate from any one of them.

**NO LIVE DEFECT FROM THE BASIS SPLIT, and I checked before raising it.**
`todayQualifiesAsCycleStart` divides a RAW `today.high` by a SPLIT-ADJUSTED
`priorClose`, which looks like the same mismatch -- **it is not.** Adjustment
restates historical prices onto the CURRENT basis, so a prior adjusted close and
today's raw price are already comparable. **My analysis mixed bases; the
production path does not.** The residual hazard is narrower: a `daily_bars` row
stored before a split carries a stale basis until refetched.

**Caveat: 8 clean symbols, n=15 and n=22.** Small, and the population shrank
*because* 89% of this universe reverse-splits. The zero residue is what carries
it, not the count.

**MY COVERAGE AUDIT HAS NO MAGNITUDE THRESHOLD, AND IT OVER-REFUSES (`622e23f`).**
`todaySoFarFromBars` refuses whenever `session_high` exceeds the bar-derived high
by more than float noise. Measured per rank band, the refusal rate is **strongly
rank-dependent in the worst direction** -- the top of the board is where it fires:

    2026-08-17   top 12 16.7%   top 25  8.0%   top 200  6.0%   all ranked  3.4%
    2026-08-18   top 12 75.0%   top 25 60.0%   top 200 39.0%   all ranked 11.9%

**The 6.4% I quoted was the universe rate and the board rate is up to 75%.** The
selection criterion is the cause: high-RVOL names are the ones that ran before we
were tracking them.

**BUT INSPECTING THE TOP 12 SPLITS THE REFUSALS INTO TWO POPULATIONS.** Gaps of
**0.1--1%** (NTWO 11.99/11.86, ENRD 10.53/10.50, SLE 7.38/7.37, SGLY, SIEB -- all
with 100--400 stored bars from 04:00) sit beside gaps of **10--66%** (TNON
10.11/6.09, TGL 4.25/2.94 on **5 bars**, PFSA, CAST). A sub-1% gap between two
sources is not *"the day's high happened in a minute we do not hold"* -- it is
noise, and the guard cannot tell it from a missed run.

⇒ **FIXED AT `410f750`: the high is tested as an INTERVAL, not a point.** `move`
is monotone in the high and the true high lies between what our bars saw and
`session_high`, so if both ends land on the same side of `CYCLE_START_MOVE_PCT`
the gap cannot change the answer. Only a straddling gap is unverifiable. And the
volume test is settled FIRST: when volume fails no high can qualify the day, so
an incomplete high is **irrelevant rather than unknown** -- that ordering is most
of the improvement.

    2026-08-18   top 12  75.0% -> 8.3%     top 25 60.0% -> 8.0%   top 200 39% -> 1.0%
    2026-08-17   top 12  16.7% -> 16.7%    top 200 6.0% -> 1.5%

**REPORT IT AS COUNTS, NOT PERCENTAGES -- Design-tmi's correction and it is
right.** The residue is **one row of twelve on 08-18 and two of twelve on
08-17**; "8.3%" and "16.7%" are the same fact dressed as a rate over n=12, and
16.7% reads worse than *two rows* while meaning the same thing. 08-17 did not
improve because those two genuinely straddle the threshold, which is the state
working rather than failing.

**AND THE BOARD RATE IS STRUCTURALLY ABOVE THE UNIVERSE RATE, not noisily above
it.** The board selects on high RVOL and high-RVOL names are the ones that ran
before the desk was tracking them, so **the selection criterion is the cause of
the refusal.** That is the cohort-selected-by-one-cause shape arriving in the
NUMERATOR. It is the part that tells him whether the rate holds on a day that is
not one of these two -- so the *why* travels with the number or neither does.

**I wrote "a defect is not a harm until the magnitude is measured" about ITHA

**THE ADJUSTMENT GUARD WAS BLIND TO VINTAGE AND IS NOW FIXED (`0821781`).
Integration-tmi found it; recording the status precisely because "checked, none
present" and "fixed" read differently to whoever arrives next.**

`dailyBarAdjustment` (`lib/research/history.ts`) returns null when a symbol's
daily bars mix adjustment bases, so nothing derives a ceiling or a prior high
from a half-restated series. It compared `SELECT DISTINCT adjustment` -- the
**label**. **Every row of `daily_bars` carries `'split'`, all 75 symbols,
measured** -- so the distinctness test returned one value unconditionally and the
guard had **no reachable path to null.** A branch that could not execute, not a
gap in coverage.

**The case it could not see:** *"split-adjusted as of August"* and *"split-adjusted
as of September"* are different bases under one word, because a reverse split
between two fetches restates one and not the other. `fetched_at` carried the
vintage and the guard did not read it. **13 of 75 symbols span two fetch dates.**

**NO CURRENT CORRUPTION, AND THAT IS NOT THE SAME AS NO FINDING.** The stored
series has no split discontinuity (largest consecutive close jump 6.46x on RCON,
3.52x on PFSA, against the 200x a mixed table would show), so the 13 are
**EXPOSED rather than wrong** -- a fetch gap only bites if a split landed inside
it. Integration-tmi's framing and it is the right one: *a guard that cannot
detect one form of the thing it was written to prevent is a finding whether or
not an instance exists today.* **It had nothing to catch, which is different from
being able to catch it.**

**Fixed by joining `fetched_at` to the distinctness test. It OVER-REFUSES on
purpose** -- all 13 now return null -- and the cheap upgrade is a `split_factor`
column, which would let it ask whether a split *actually* intervened. `db.ts:710`
migrates one in; **the local store genuinely lacks it, verified not assumed.**
Five tests, none existed before; label-only kills exactly one of five as
predicted.

**AND I OVER-CORRECTED ON THEIR RE-FETCH.** I said the split re-fetch "was not
needed for the reason given". **Wrong:** they ordered it off a directly observed
header mismatch -- `adjustment: raw` in the file against a store and a rule
running `'split'` -- and **thresholds must be derived in the basis the rule runs
in whether 67 symbols drift or none do.** My withdrawn 67-of-75 was evidence for
how bad it was, never for whether it was real. *Retracting a magnitude does not
retract the decision it happened to support* -- which is the mirror of
"disavowed the result and kept the conclusion", and I walked into the reflection.

**THE CALIBRATION DATA IS AUDITED AND SOUND, by a method that does not compare
the two files -- because the method I used to find MSS could not have.**

I found MSS's truncation by diffing raw against split. **A symbol truncated in
BOTH files is invisible to that**, and Ops reported 0 errors on the raw fetch
too, so the split file's only evidence of completeness was that it differed from
a file now known to be broken. **That is not evidence.** Integration-tmi caught
it; same wrong-arm shape as the positive control that proved traded rows were
detectable when the claim was about untraded ones.

**THE DISTINCTION THAT MAKES A CONTIGUITY AUDIT POSSIBLE:**

    TRUNCATION   dense coverage that STOPS EARLY      density ~1.0, then a gap
    A THIN NAME  sparse THROUGHOUT                    low density, or starts late

Audited each file against the 62-session window itself, flagging density >= 0.9
with a >= 5-session tail gap:

    RAW   (positive control)   MSS  ends 07-24  45/45 dates  density 1.00
                               gap 17 sessions  last day 9 bars vs typical 14
    SPLIT (the calibration data)   no truncation signature found

**The positive control is the part that makes the silence mean anything** -- the
detector demonstrably catches the known case, and `VOGX` (5 dates), `FSHP` (18)
and `NTWO` (21) are correctly NOT flagged in either file, so it separates sparse
from truncated rather than just counting rows. **MSS is complete in the split
file: 62 dates, full range.**

⇒ **Derive thresholds on `alpaca-1hour-split-...`. The raw file is the
unadjusted record only, and it is incomplete for MSS.**

**AND THE MISTAKE WORTH KEEPING IS SMALLER THAN THE FIX.** MSS appeared in my
residue table as *"not in hourly file"* and I wrote that down as a fact **about
the symbol** rather than a question about the **fetch**. *The data's absence
described the instrument and I attributed it to the world.*

**THE FRAME CHANGE DOES NOT FIX `isCycleStart`, AND THIS MATTERS TO THE RULING
HE IS BEING ASKED FOR.** Integration-tmi drew the right consequence from the
volume asymmetry -- the two halves of `CYCLE_START` are measured over different
windows -- but attributed it to the HIGH. **It is the CLOSE**, and that is a
worse problem than a frame:

    isCycleStart (cycle.ts)   move gate = closeChangePct   prior CLOSE -> this CLOSE
                              vol  gate = dailyRvol        daily_bars.volume

**The volume reaches past 16:00 (measured NOT RTH-only, 3 of 2,747) and the close
is a 16:00 point.** So a premarket runner puts extended-session volume into the
RVOL gate and a regular-session move into the move gate.

⇒ **AND WIDENING THE FRAME CANNOT REPAIR IT.** An extended frame gives an
extended high and an extended close -- a 20:00 last print. **A close is a point in
time, so no frame makes it see a premarket spike that faded by then.** A name
that runs to +80% at 08:00 and is flat by 16:00 has a small close-to-close move
in EVERY frame. `isCycleStart` is structurally blind to intraday extremes, not
merely windowed wrongly.

⇒ **The sibling is not affected, and this is why it was built high-based.**
`todayQualifiesAsCycleStart` measures the move on the HIGH, which is what makes
it *strictly more permissive than its settled parent* and what makes it catch the
spike-and-fade day the parent loses. **Already recorded as a property of the
sibling; now it is also the reason the frame ruling does not reach the parent.**

**So the ruling splits three ways, not two:** the frame change fixes the
high-based quantities (`cycleHigh`, `retracementPct`, the sibling's input); it
does nothing for `isCycleStart`'s move gate; and whether the PARENT should become
high-based is a separate question nobody has put to him.

**QCLS IS FULLY DOCUMENTED AND MY "CANNOT REPRODUCE" WAS A SIMULATION ERROR.**
`docs/threads/ops.md:10297` — **INCIDENT 2026-09-16 12:22 ET**, his screenshot,
read from the store: rank 3, price 1.635, reference close **0.4413 (09-15)**,
`percent_change` 270.5, `session_high` 1.76, halted LUDP. Badge read
`BACKSIDE $5.49 -> $1.35 HALTED`. **The $5.49 is 2026-05-14.**

**AND THE RULE WAS NEVER WRONG.** QCLS's latest daily bar was **09-15**.
`ensureDailyHistory` writes nothing before 20:00 ET and `readDailyBars` excludes
unfinished bars, so today was not in the input. **The settled arc 5.49 -> 0.44
genuinely IS backside as of yesterday's close.** The badge's left number is
`max(cycleHigh, sessionHigh)` = 5.49 and its right is the live price, so the
board printed **a live price against a dead run, in red, on the name ranked
third.**

⇒ **MY FOUR SCENARIOS ALL INCLUDED TODAY'S BAR IN THE SERIES, WHICH IS THE ONE
THING THE REAL INPUT EXCLUDES.** I built each series through "today" and asked
why the rule misbehaved. It does not misbehave — it never sees today. *I
simulated the system I was describing rather than the one that runs, and
concluded the incident had not happened.* **Second-hand was not the problem; my
harness was.**

⇒ **AND OPS'S FIX SHAPE IS EXACTLY WHAT SHIPPED.** Theirs, 09-16: *"a provisional
TODAY bar (from `ticker_session`'s live anchors, session high, price, cumulative
volume) in the cycle input during the session, so a name up 270% from yesterday's
close classifies as a new run."* That is `todaySoFarFromBars` +
`todayQualifiesAsCycleStart`, wired at `e48a2ca`. **The justification stands and
the feature answers it.**

⇒ **IT ALSO SETTLES HIGH-VS-CLOSE FOR THE SIBLING BY NECESSITY.** At 12:22 ET
QCLS had a `session_high` of 1.76 and **no close at all** — intraday there is no
close. Measuring the move on the high was not a preference. *The open question
was only ever about the SETTLED parent, and that one remains unreproduced and
withdrawn on its own merits.*

**HIS CONTINUATION MODEL IS ALREADY THE IMPLEMENTATION.**
2026-09-19, his words: *"i dont think price determines a continuation, for me its
volume, its the same run if RVOL has not returned to its original state."*

**That is what `resolveCycle` does.** `wentQuiet` (3 sessions at RVOL <= 2) is
tested BEFORE the backside branch, and `wentQuiet && sessionsSinceHigh > 10`
retires the cycle entirely. **Price only sets the phase WITHIN a live cycle.**
And RVOL self-rebases, so *"returned to its original state"* is literally RVOL
~= 1: a name held at 3x for 40 sessions has a 3x median, so its RVOL reads 1 and
the cycle expires. Verified by construction, not by reading.

**FOUR SCENARIOS, NONE REPRODUCES `BACKSIDE $5.49` AGAINST A FOUR-MONTH-OLD HIGH:**

    quiet then re-ignition        -> NO_CYCLE, then a NEW cycle at today's high
    sustained elevated volume     -> RVOL rebases to 1, cycle expires
    gaps in daily_bars            -> zero symbols of 75 have any internal gap
    intraday spike, modest close  -> BACKSIDE, but against TODAY's high

The last is defensible rather than defective: a name that touched 6.90 and closed
3.22 has given back 62% of its advance.

⇒ **THE HIGH-VS-CLOSE QUESTION STAYS WITHDRAWN, but for a narrower reason than I
first gave.** It is a question about `isCycleStart` on SETTLED days, and the QCLS
incident is about today being absent — so QCLS never evidenced it either way. No
scenario I can build shows the settled rule misbehaving on a complete series.

**THE STRUCTURAL FACT, NOW CONFIRMED AS THE ACTUAL CAUSE RATHER THAN A FALLBACK:**
`readDailyBars` defaults to `unfinished: 'EXCLUDE'` (`history.ts:149`), so
**today's bar is not in the cycle input at all.** A name up 270% right now has
its cycle computed as of YESTERDAY. That is structural, and the 09-16 incident is
exactly it. **The feature stands and so does its headline example.**

**ONE THING THE INCIDENT DOES NOT EXPLAIN AND NOBODY HAS ASKED:** why the May
cycle was still live on 09-15 at all. `wentQuiet && sessionsSinceHigh > 10`
retires a cycle, and 5.49 on 05-14 to 0.44 on 09-15 is four months past the high.
**So `wentQuiet` must have been false throughout** — a name bleeding out can hold
RVOL above 2x for a long time. Not a defect on its face, and unexamined.

### OPEN AND MINE

**The cycle sibling — designed across three seats, UNBUILT.** QCLS showed
`BACKSIDE $5.49` in red while up 270%; the $5.49 is a four-month-old run. The
supersession rule already exists (`cycle.ts:108-114`) and cannot see today.
Three parts: a **high-based** move test (monotone, so the latch is free and needs
no stored state), the provisional bar `{close, high, volume}` with `settled:
false` letting the module use its **own** denominators, and a bad-print guard
comparing the high against **the close of the bar that set it** — which makes it
immune to the asymmetric reseed and structurally unable to run on a seeded high.
**Design waits on one latched flag meaning *today HAS qualified this session*.**

**A CONSTRAINT ON THAT BUILD, and it is the reason this is in the file rather
than only at the type.** `548acf8` added per-session highs beside the day-wide
one. **They are never seeded** — `SessionSeed` has no plural fields, the seed path
touches only `sessionHigh`/`sessionLow`, and the maps initialise all-null and
rebuild from post-restart bars alone.

```
day-wide sessionHigh   SEEDED from dailyBar.h   RTH restart: SURVIVES   premarket: LOST
per-session highs      NOT SEEDED               RTH restart: LOST       premarket: LOST
```

> **THE LATCH MUST READ THE DAY-WIDE VALUE.** Not because it is sturdier but
> because it is the right question: `closeChangePct` compares a DAY close to the
> PRIOR DAY's close, so *"has today qualified as a cycle start"* is day-level. A
> latch on `sessionHighs.premarket` would look more careful, stop surviving an
> RTH restart, and silently widen the population Design's board statement was
> shaped for.

**And the failure mode is the one this file warns about, arriving as a FRESH
value rather than a stale one: it does not error, it answers LOW.** A restart at
10:30 gives an RTH high measured from 10:30 and nothing on the board says so.
Design-tmi caught it a day after I shipped it — **I had written the rule to check
exactly this the day before, then shipped a per-session accumulator without
asking what reseeds it.** Documented at the type in `dbae021`; seeding them is
not possible from a snapshot (a daily bar has one high, no session breakdown),
and the unwired `lib/market/replay.ts` would repair these and the anchors
together.

**Untraced:** whether `sheetPriorOmitted` persists readably. If it does, *"how
many stored dossiers saw a prior"* sizes the back-catalogue exposure, and it is a
different number from both the unmeasurable disagreement rate and the control
arm's magnitude.

**Scoped to Ops, mine to have scoped:** the selector self-report, and the
`rvol_rank`-seeded focused set.

**FILING-DERIVED FLOAT: A NUMBER IS NOT REACHABLE, BUT BOTH TAILS ARE.** Asked
by Integration-tmi as the whole critical path of the Sheet migration's Phase C,
and the answer was already in the type rather than needing a study.

`FloatBasis` has exactly two members. `SHEET_VENDOR` is the vendor number with no
published methodology. `FILED_SHARES_OUTSTANDING` is documented in its own
comment as **"an UPPER bound on float, never a float -- every share an insider
holds is inside it."** Filings publish shares OUTSTANDING; float is outstanding
minus affiliate and restricted holdings, and that subtrahend lives in 13D/G,
Forms 3/4/5 and the proxy, **none of which this desk collects.** So there is a
collection gap behind the collection gap and closing it is not Phase C.

**BUT PILLAR 5 ASKS *IS THE FLOAT LOW*, NOT *WHAT IS IT*, and the desk owns two
one-sided instruments that between them cover both tails:**

    float bound   LOW_FLOAT_CEILING = 10M     CONCLUSIVE WHEN LOW
    floor ratio   supply.ts:288-291           CONCLUSIVE WHEN HIGH

Silent in the middle band, and silent on the number for everyone. **Coverage of
the bound is the figure that matters: 46.9% within `FILED_SHARES_CURRENT_DAYS`
(45), 50.2% at 90 -- 211 issuers, 2026-08-21.** So about half of names return
`CANNOT_VERIFY` or `NO_FILED_COUNT`. A month old, a sample, not live.

⇒ **Retiring task 1 replaces a NUMBER with a two-tailed verdict, conclusive at
the extremes, silent in the middle, available for about half of names.** Not a
like-for-like substitution, and he should hear it in those words before ruling.

**AND PHASE C HAS A HAZARD THAT FAILS REASSURINGLY.** `assessFloatBound` adjusts
the filed count by a cumulative split factor, and its comment records that an
**inverted factor manufactures proof** -- on a forward-split name it understates
the count and returns a **false PROVEN**, i.e. a confident low-float badge on a
name that is not. Direction was verified against ZOOZ (162.00M / 20.00 = 8.10M),
not derived. Any Phase C work re-checks that across split types first.

**THE PREMARKET HALF IS NOT RULED. DO NOT DERIVE AGAINST IT.**

This is the one thing in this file most likely to be read wrong, because the two
halves sit in different sections. **He ruled AFTER-HOURS in, when "the frame"
meant the evening.** The premarket exclusion was measured afterwards and is the
LARGER correction -- and it has been put to him, not answered.

    AFTER-HOURS in the frame    RULED, not in doubt
    PREMARKET   in the frame    MEASURED, PUT TO HIM, UNANSWERED

Integration-tmi recorded *"ruled yes, and wider than asked"* in their own charter
(`045efd3`) and then withdrew it: **the widening was their inference.** They had
told him the scope would grow if the data confirmed; he has not answered that
part. **Told and silent is not approved** -- the same rule I broke earlier the
same night by telling Design a render was "seen and approved".

⇒ **So `0.5` and `2.0` may be re-derived against an AFTER-HOURS-inclusive frame
once he confirms, and MUST NOT be re-derived against a premarket-inclusive one
until he rules the morning in.** Deriving against an unruled frame would bake an
unapproved scope into two constants that then look calibrated -- which is exactly
what the FRAME WARNING at their definition sites exists to prevent.

**AND A THIRD QUESTION IS OPEN THAT NEITHER RULING COVERS:** whether
`isCycleStart`'s move gate should measure the HIGH instead of the close. No frame
reaches it -- see above. Also unanswered.

**HE RULED THE FRAME AFTER-HOURS-INCLUSIVE (via Integration-tmi), calibrate
against the last three months. THE RULING SPLITS IN TWO AND ONLY HALF IS
BLOCKED.**

**Not blocked -- the live rule.** `ahHigh` already exists on the runtime, so
`highCeiling` becoming `max(session_high, ahHigh)` needs no history at all. The
sibling can be built in the new frame immediately; the constants simply keep
their current values until re-derived.

**Blocked -- the constants.** `BACKSIDE_RETRACEMENT = 0.5` and
`SUPERRUNNER_ADVANCE = 2.0` were calibrated on AH-excluded daily highs, and
three months of AH-inclusive highs is not in the store: `minute_bars` holds two
dates locally and ~20 in production under retention.

**AND THERE IS NO EXTENDED-HOURS DAILY BAR, read off the parameter list rather
than recalled.** `/v2/stocks/bars` takes `symbols`, `timeframe`, `start`, `end`,
`limit`, `adjustment`, `asof`, `feed`, `currency`, `page_token`, `sort` -- **no
session parameter, no extended-hours parameter.** `feed` picks the SOURCE, not
the window: `sip` / `iex` / `otc` / `boats`, and **`boats` is Blue Ocean ATS
*overnight* data (20:00-04:00), a different session on a different feed.** So the
AH high is unobtainable at daily granularity at any parameter.

⇒ **BUT THE BACKFILL MAY BE ~60x SMALLER THAN MINUTE BARS.** The derivation needs
a daily AH-inclusive high, not minute resolution. `1Hour` bars would give it at
~16 bars per symbol-day against ~960. **Unverified whether hourly covers
16:00-20:00** -- one request against a known AH runner settles it, and that is a
fetch decision rather than an analysis one. *If hourly carries AH, three months
is a modest backfill and not a data project.*

**AND THE CLOSE MUST MOVE WITH THE HIGH.** Integration-tmi flagged it and it is
worse than a display bug: `givebackPct` AND `retracementPct` both divide against
`latestClose`, and `retracementPct`'s own docstring says *"This, not
givebackPct, decides the phase."* **So a half-changed frame MISCLASSIFIES the
name** -- an AH runner that holds reads as having given it all back -- and
deriving `0.5` against that bakes the artefact into the constant. The close must
become the extended session's last print. **Costs nothing extra in data**: the
same backfill supplying each day's AH high supplies that day's AH last print.

**HIS RULING, 2026-09-19: THE VENDOR FLOAT STAYS ON THE DESKTOP TASK AND MUST
NEVER MOVE SERVER-SIDE.** *"keep it as is - but i dont want to run this on a gpt
task from the outside. it runs from my desktop gpt, not from the api."*

**So task 1 is NOT retired and NOT migrated.** The distinction he is drawing is
the one the terms turn on: **a person using the platform through their own
desktop assistant is personal, manual use; a scheduled server-side fetch is
not.** The float channel stays where it is.

⇒ **STANDING CONSTRAINT: no worker, no API route and no scheduled job may fetch
from `stockanalysis.com`.** Not as a "temporary" backfill, not behind a cache,
not once. The volume is small enough (~150/day) that automating it will keep
looking like an easy win to whoever reads the sizing without the terms -- which
is why the sizing and this constraint live in the same file.

⇒ **AND IT CHANGES THE MIGRATION'S SHAPE, NOT JUST ITS ORDER.** Integration-tmi
had float as the blocker on retiring task 1. It is not a blocker any more because
**the task is not being retired** -- so the remaining Sheet work is the judgement
and prose groups, and Phase C becomes an addition beside the vendor number rather
than a replacement for it. His *"post vendor float and then derived float, i'd be
interested to see the differences"* is exactly that: two channels, two origins,
side by side, and only one of them is ours to compute.

**THE VENDOR FLOAT FETCH IS NOT A COST ITEM. THE SOURCE'S TERMS PROHIBIT IT.**
Integration-tmi asked me to cost it as "the only genuinely new thing in the whole
migration". Read live at `stockanalysis.com/terms-of-use/` on 2026-09-19 and
quoted exactly:

> *"**Automated access.** The platform and any account on it are for personal,
> manual use via the web browser or mobile app. **You may not use bots, scripts,
> scrapers, browser automations or any other automated or programmatic methods
> to access the platform, collect data from it, or download data in bulk.** This
> does not apply to search engines, AI agents, or other crawlers that follow our
> robots.txt file. **You can also not use our content or data to build a
> competing database or product**, or to use the data to train AI or machine
> learning models."*

**TWO SEPARATE CLAUSES AND THE SECOND IS THE HARDER ONE.** The first bars the
access method -- a worker fetching 200 names a day is squarely "scripts... to
collect data from it". There is a carve-out for *"search engines, AI agents, or
other crawlers that follow our robots.txt"*, and `robots.txt` disallows only
`/e/` and `/p/`, so the stock pages are crawlable — **but a scheduled worker is
not a search engine or a general crawler.** The second clause bars the **USE**
regardless of how the data was obtained: TMI Trader would display that float to
paying customers, which is building a product on their content.

**⇒ THIS IS A BUSINESS AND LEGAL DECISION, NOT AN ENGINEERING ESTIMATE**, and I
am not going to scope it as one. The volume is trivial (below) and the volume was
never the constraint.

**THE SIZING, SO IT IS ON RECORD IF A LICENSED ROUTE OPENS:** 200 names per day
in the top 200; 475 distinct symbols across three stored dates, so roughly 150
new per day at that churn. With a cache and a TTL it is ~150 fetches/day. *Small
enough that a licensed feed would be cheap and a scrape was never justified by
scale.*

**AND IT MAY DESCRIBE THE CURRENT STATE, WHICH HE SHOULD KNOW.** The float on the
board today comes from a scheduled ChatGPT task reading that same site. **That
task may sit inside the "AI agents" carve-out where a worker would not** -- I am
not asserting which, because it turns on their reading and not on ours. Either
way the second clause is about use, and the use is the same today as it would be
after the migration.

**⇒ IT STRENGTHENS PHASE C RATHER THAN BLOCKING THE MIGRATION.** SEC filings are
public domain and carry none of this. His ruling was *"post vendor float and then
derived float, i'd be interested to see the differences"* -- **the derived half is
unaffected and buildable now**, and `assessFloat` (`float.ts:326`) already IS the
containment test Integration described: it returns `IMPOSSIBLE` when a claimed
float exceeds a current filed count. What is missing is only the vendor number,
and that is the half with the problem.

**SHOULD THE QUIET TEST ALSO HAVE AN ABSOLUTE FLOOR? HIS QUESTION, MEASURED,
AND THE ANSWER IS YES — THE THRESHOLD IS HIS.**

RVOL is self-relative, so **it can certify a name as "still in play" on volume
that is absolutely untradeable.** Measured on the 2026-08-23 production snapshot,
43,692 rows, of the 4,142 reading RVOL >= 2:

    under $50k traded all day     352   ( 8.5%)
    under $100k                   607   (14.7%)
    under $250k                 1,131   (27.3%)
    under $1M                   2,139   (51.6%)      p05 = $29,809

**More than half of "still busy" rows traded under a million dollars**, and the
bottom five percent under thirty thousand. A four-month-old cycle staying live on
$30k of tape is the same defect as the consecutive-sessions one, from the other
side.

**WHAT A FLOOR WOULD COST, against board-visible rows:**

    floor      cuts of RVOL>=2 rows      cuts of board top-200 rows
    $25,000            4.1%                       0.42%
    $50,000            8.5%                       2.17%
    $100,000          14.7%                       5.33%
    $200,000          24.1%                      11.67%
    $500,000          39.5%                      23.00%

**The ratio turns above $50k** — board impact 2.5x for population 1.7x. And the
board TOP 12 never trades under **$736,363**, so any floor in this range cannot
touch the names he actually looks at.

**DOLLARS, NOT SHARES, and the reason is the frame rule.** He said "daily
volume"; share count is price-dependent — 2M shares of a $0.30 name is $600k and
real, the same 2M at $0.02 is $40k and is not. **Dollar volume is the only
absolute measure that means the same thing across a $1-$20 universe.**

**AND IT MUST BE A DISJUNCTION, NOT A REPLACEMENT.** The run is over when the
typical day is back to the name's OWN normal (RVOL, which adapts per name and
catches re-basing) **OR** below an absolute floor (which catches "busy relative
to nothing"). Each catches what the other cannot.

**Safe for fresh runs by construction:** `wentQuiet` already requires
`sessionsInCycle > shadowSessions`, so a name that ran today cannot go quiet
whatever its dollar volume.

⇒ **UNBUILT. He said "i'm not sure", and a threshold that changes cycle labels on
his board is his to set, not mine to pick.** My recommendation is **$50,000**:
it removes 8.5% of the untradeable-but-busy population for 2.17% of board rows,
sits below the turn in the ratio, and is an order of magnitude under the TOP 12
minimum.

- *"retention is 3"* → **20**.
- *"the guard cannot flicker"* → **it can.** Monotone holds for RVOL and not for
  the conjunction; `percent_change` moves both ways at 1s. Latched now.
- *"the board can distinguish traded from cannot-say"* → **it could not**; all
  nine columns were null and the set read `undefined`.
- *"no `sheet` source proves the anchor is right"* → **vacuous**; no code writes
  that value, so the query could not have found one.
- *"0 of 800 board-visible names were untraded"* → **vacuous**; board visibility
  requires volume, so the population was empty by construction.
- *"the day-wide `sessionHigh` SURVIVES an RTH restart"* -> **only once the daily
  bar has rolled**, which is itself unmeasured. Integration-tmi flagged it in a
  comment whose whole purpose was telling the next seat which input is safe. It
  degrades to LOST and never to a stale high, so nothing built on it became
  unsafe -- but it was stated flatly and would have been read as a guarantee.
- *"the disagreement rate is unmeasurable"* → **true, and it was the wrong
  number.** The control arm's magnitude is measurable. *"Unmeasurable" is usually
  "not that number, this one."*

### The basis fetch — the design, so you do not have to re-derive it

`bc15588` renders on zero rows because its basis check needs a per-session split
factor, and those exist only where `ensureDeepHistory` has run.
`deepHistoryDue` gates on **rank ≤ 10 AND a price above every stored high** — a
blue-sky breakout. Replayed over every stored ticker-session on the 08-23
snapshot: the gate would ever fire for **11 symbols**, 2 of which hold a
dossier, and **0 of the 55 rows that would render a pair.**

**The fix: decouple the dual-adjustment fetch from the blue-sky gate.** A basis
fetch should run once for any *researched* ticker; keep the blue-sky deep fetch
exactly as it is. Cost is **~231 symbols × 2 daily-bar REST calls**, one-off,
then only new names — splits are rare enough that it is close to once per ticker
forever. **Alpaca calls, not model calls.** Ops prices the volume before it runs.

**Do not weaken the guard to make the number appear.** The whole point is that a
wrong basis is invisible at 150%: 45.5% of rows in the 100–200% band carry a
reverse split and still look plausible.

**EXECUTED 2026-09-02, `3379809`, with two riders the design turned out to
need — both measured before building, neither weakening the guard:**

- **The pair reads its factors at FULL stored depth, not from the 90-bar cycle
  window.** The dates the basis check compares are filing dates, and on the
  08-23 snapshot **122 of 239 dated supply blocks (block-denominated) — and
  every dated block on 98 of 157 block-holding tickers (ticker-denominated) —
  sit beyond that window**; the filed denominator's median age is 82 days with
  39% over 180 (item 14's measurement). Factors clipped to the cycle window
  would hand the guard nulls for exactly the operands the fetch was approved to
  make comparable. `readSplitFactors` in `lib/research/history.ts`, `asOf`-
  bounded like the cycle bars.
- **`computeSupplyPair` refuses to extrapolate a factor past the series end.**
  `splitFactorAt` falls back to the nearest EARLIER session — right inside the
  series, wrong past its end: an operand dated after the last covered session
  would inherit that session's factor, and a split in the gap would make two
  incomparable operands read as COMPARABLE. Beyond coverage is
  `BASIS_UNVERIFIABLE`: a wrong answer becomes a missing one. Consequence a
  successor should expect rather than rediscover: **an established basis decays
  for actively re-analysed names** — operands dated after the establishment
  fetch go unverifiable, visibly, in the exclusion reasons. The honest fix if
  it starts to bite is a bounded re-fetch trigger, a new (small) spend
  decision, not a wider fallback.

**The predicate is the FACTOR, not the deep-source marker** — the shallow
refresh overwrites `source` on every row it touches while `split_factor` is
COALESCEd, so a source-based test would re-arm forever on any listing younger
than the shallow window. Pinned in `tests/research/basisFetch.test.ts`,
including the decoupling itself (due where `deepHistoryDue` says not-due).

**The rendered-coverage number does not exist yet and must not be promised.**
It is measurable only after the backfill runs on the migrated store and names
re-analyse — the stored pairs in old dossiers do not retroactively change.

### The condition that binds, and is not a property of the code

**Pin the run to `data/market-prod-2026-08-23.db`.** `readSources` does not
filter by date — `activeOnly` is its only option — so a replay bundles *every*
source a ticker has, including sources collected **after** the session being
replayed. Run against a freshly taken database next week, the re-derived grades
would carry look-ahead, and **Q1 would be invalid in a way nobody would see**:
the grades would look ordinary and would have been formed from news that had not
happened yet.

It is safe today **by accident of timing, not by design** — exactly one source,
across one ticker, in that snapshot was published after 21 August. If this run
slips and someone re-takes the snapshot, either re-check that count or add
as-of source filtering first.

This is written down here because it will not hold on its own. Nothing in the
code enforces it, no test covers it, and the snapshot's filename is the only
thing standing between a valid result and a plausible invalid one.

### RETRACTED 2026-08-23: the prior was never shown to move the grade

*Retracted by Research; enumerated here by Integration, because the claim stood
for several hours and was copied into four documents across three threads while
it stood.*

**What is withdrawn:** "removing the Sheet's prior changed the catalyst grade on
2 of 6 names against a control variance of 0 of 6". At **four runs per arm**,
**0 of 6** tickers are stable-in-both-arms-but-different. The two reported as
moved are the two that vary *within the control set anyway*. The original figure
came from single runs and could not separate the prior's effect from the model's
own variance.

**What survives, and it is not small.** `sheetPrior` **does** reach the
interpreter on every call — that is a code fact, traced through `bundle.ts:426`
to `buildInput` at `:102` and `JSON.stringify(bundle)` at `:107`, on the main
path called at `:188`. **The exposure is confirmed. The effect is not
demonstrated.** Those are different statements and the second does not erase the
first.

**Do not over-correct to "there is no problem".** A null at n=6, on a field now
known to be 2-of-6 unstable on identical evidence, is a weak instrument. It says
the earlier positive was indistinguishable from noise; it does not say the prior
is inert. The honest state is **unmeasured**, not **clean**.

**A second revision travels with it and has its own consequences.**
`catalystGrade` was reported **stable at 0 of 6** on fixed evidence, off two
runs. Four runs make it **2 of 6 unstable**. Any argument resting on catalyst
being the stable field needs re-examining — including R&D's reasoning that its
52% stored-record figure is dominated by real evidence change *because* catalyst
moved on the identical 29 pairs and catalyst was stable. That premise is weaker
than when it was written. R&D has been told directly.

Q1 register row and the ANSWERED block), and
`docs/rnd/2026-08-23-outcome-capture.md`. Each thread owns its own correction;

**14. Float: derived from filings, shipping with its own confidence signal. One
piece of work, not two.** *Decided by Integration 2026-08-24 under the
order-and-process delegation, with the route reversed from what Integration
recommended earlier.*

**The reversal, and the evidence that caused it.** I recommended the vendor
route first, on the grounds that it *reproduces the number already on the
board, so nothing changes*. **58 hand-pulled names then showed that number is
arithmetically impossible on one name in six**, and on ADRs the unit test fires
on 8 of 11. "Reproduces what is on the board" turned out to mean "reproduces
something demonstrably broken", and no vendor publishes its rules, so there is
no reading under which StockAnalysis is safer than Scanz.

So: **derive from filings, as the trader originally chose.** Not because the
data is better — that is unproven — but because **it is the only route where
the rules are visible and a failure is detectable.**

**And it is one project, not a float followed by a check.** Deriving from
filings puts shares outstanding in hand at the moment float is computed, so the
consistency test is free rather than plumbed. More important, **the signal is
what makes the derived number honest**: it lets the desk say *I cannot compute
this one* instead of guessing, which is the whole difference between this and a
vendor.

Ships with, non-negotiably:

- **`float_basis` from the first row**, per R&D's rule. Never retrofitted.
- **`float > shares_outstanding` → refuse — BUT ONLY WHEN THE DENOMINATOR IS
  CURRENT.** *Qualifier added by Research 2026-08-24 before the build, and
  accepted by Integration under the delegation. Without it the rule inverts the
  signal.* The filed share count is old for much of the universe — measured
  across 209 issuers: **39% over 180 days, median 82 days**, oldest STG at 3,065
  days. A company that has issued shares since its last filing **legitimately**
  has a float exceeding the filed count.

  **And the error runs the wrong way: the rule fires hardest on the names that
  dilute hardest**, because those are the ones whose count has grown since
  filing. The desk would go blind on pillar 5 precisely where supply risk is
  highest — an inverse correlation with what the field is for.

  So: **carry the denominator's age, and on a stale one report *cannot verify*
  rather than refusing.** Same honest answer the design is built around. And
  `shares_outstanding_as_of` ships beside the count per R&D's basis rule — a
  count without its date is a different quantity from a count with one.

  **`YJ` is the single best test case**: oldest-five staleness at 2,790 days
  *and* the ADR the classification records as ordinary. It fails on both axes at
  once.
- **Ratio under ~2% → refuse as a probable unit mismatch.** Cannot be gated on
  `ADR_ADS`: YJ is an ADR the classification records as ordinary, so the test
  stands on the ratio alone.
- **A derivative must not inherit its underlying's float.** `ENRDW` carried
  ENRD's verbatim, and warrants are exactly what a low-float runner's structure
  contains.
- **No split component.** Splits do not discriminate — all 9 flagged names have
  one and so do 13 of 25 clean ones. A split term would be the part that
  misleads.

**Open and unsettled inside it**, flagged by R&D and not to be quietly resolved:
13G filers are passive institutions whose shares belong in the float. Subtract
them and float is understated across the board — a false positive on pillar 5,
which is the dangerous direction.

Design renders it afterwards, including what a **refused** float looks like on a
row. That is a real design question and it is not this thread's.
