**120. BOTH DELETION PATHS FOR `minute_bars` ARE REFUTED FROM CODE, SO THE 09-04
BARS WERE NEVER WRITTEN. A NEGATIVE RESULT, WHICH IS THE ONLY KIND I SHOULD BE
OFFERING ON THIS AFTER TONIGHT.**

*The missing bars are the last finding standing. There are exactly **two** places
in the codebase that remove a `minute_bars` row — enumerated, not sampled:*

```
lib/market/store/repo.ts:281   DELETE FROM minute_bars WHERE trading_date NOT IN (...)
lib/market/store/db.ts:1124    DELETE FROM ticker_session; DELETE FROM minute_bars; DELETE FROM desk_events;
```

*Every other mention is a `SELECT`, the `CREATE TABLE`, the index, or one
`INSERT` at `repo.ts:163`.*

### 1. RETENTION CANNOT REMOVE 09-04 WHILE KEEPING 09-02 AND 09-03

`pruneRetention` (`runtime.ts:1687`) builds its keep-list from
`retainedMinuteBarDates` → `recentMinuteBarDates(db, N)`:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT trading_date FROM minute_bars ORDER BY trading_date DESC LIMIT ?
```

**The keep-list is the N MOST RECENT dates PRESENT, plus `this.tradingDate`
added explicitly** — the comment says why: *"so a live session's incoming bars
are never the thing being deleted."*

**09-04 IS MORE RECENT THAN 09-03 AND 09-02.** Any pass that saw 09-04 rows would
have ranked them **first** in the keep-list. **Retention deletes the OLDEST; this
is the wrong direction**, and it would have taken 09-02 before it touched 09-04.
*It also guards `keep.length === 0` → delete nothing, so an empty table cannot
cascade.*

### 2. THE MODE-SWITCH WIPE CANNOT BE IT EITHER, AND `ticker_session` PROVES IT

`claimStoreForMode` deletes `ticker_session`, `minute_bars` and `desk_events`
**in one transaction**, when the store's recorded `market_mode` differs from the
one claiming it.

**09-04's `ticker_session` ROWS SURVIVE — 7,757 DEAD plus 1,015 UNKNOWN.** *A wipe
would have taken them in the same transaction as the bars.* **So this path did
not run after those rows were written, and it cannot explain bars missing from
the same date.**

### SO: NO DELETION PATH EXPLAINS IT. THE ROWS WERE NEVER INSERTED.

**That converges with the two independent readings already on the table:**

- **Ops's**, from the backups: one persistence failure, starting 09-04.
- **Mine**, from `activity.ts:259` — an empty map returns `UNKNOWN` and cannot
  return `DEAD`, so **`DEAD 7,757` proves the feed was delivering.**

**FEED ALIVE + NO DELETION PATH ⇒ THE WRITE AT `repo.ts:163` IS WHERE TO LOOK.**
*Not the retention job, not a mode switch, not the vendor.*

### WHAT THIS IS NOT

**IT IS NOT A MECHANISM AND I AM NOT OFFERING ONE.** *Four hours ago I asserted a
cause on a comparison that did not hold, and it took building the instrument that
could refute me to kill it.* **Two eliminations and a narrowed search is what I
can defend from code tonight; the write path itself is Ops's file and Ops's
call.**

**AND THE ELIMINATIONS ARE FALSIFIABLE IN ONE STEP EACH:** a retention pass that
deleted 09-04 would have logged `[store] pruned N minute bars`, and a mode switch
would have left no 09-04 `ticker_session` rows at all.

**121. THE FINGERPRINT-MOVEMENT QUERY IS UNANSWERABLE, AND THE REASON IS THAT
`fetched_at` IDENTIFIES A ROW RATHER THAN A PASS. CLOSING IT AS A NEGATIVE.**

*My last genuinely open item: **per `(ticker, trading_date)`, distinct `fetched_at`
moments bringing new source rows against the number of times the job was asked.***

### THE FIRST RUN LOOKED LIKE AN ANSWER AND WAS BACKWARDS

```
(ticker, trading_date) pairs with at least one job : 323
jobs asked                                         : 964
distinct fetched_at values on those pairs          : 3,960
```

**FOUR "FETCH MOMENTS" PER JOB.** *A number that says collection ran four times
for every time it was asked is not a finding, it is a broken denominator* — so I
checked the numerator before writing it down.

### `fetched_at` IS MINTED PER ROW FOR THE DOMINANT SOURCE TYPE

| source_type | rows | distinct `fetched_at` | ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **SEC_FILING** | **3,253** | **3,247** | **1.00** |
| SEC_SUBMISSIONS | 257 | 257 | 1.00 |
| SEC_COMPANY_FACTS | 211 | 211 | 1.00 |
| SEC_EXHIBIT | 878 | 256 | 0.29 |
| COMPANY_NEWSROOM | 105 | 35 | 0.33 |
| COMPANY_IR | 93 | 34 | 0.37 |

**`sec/collector.ts:453` calls `new Date().toISOString()` PER FILING**, so every
`SEC_FILING` row gets its own millisecond. **`catalyst/collector.ts:412` uses a
single `now` for the pass**, so exhibits and company sources share one.

**SO THE COLUMN MEANS DIFFERENT THINGS IN DIFFERENT ROWS OF THE SAME TABLE**, and
for the two-thirds of rows that are `SEC_FILING` it means *"when this row was
made"*, not *"when the pass ran"*.

**TRUNCATION DOES NOT RESCUE IT.** 4,882 rows carry 1,329 distinct seconds and
283 distinct minutes. Rounding to the minute would merge genuinely separate
passes and still split any pass that straddled a boundary. **A pass has no
identifier at all.**

### SO THE QUESTION FAILS TWICE OVER, INDEPENDENTLY

1. **Item 110:** a pass that added nothing writes no row and leaves no timestamp,
   **so unproductive passes are invisible.**
2. **This:** a pass that DID add rows cannot be recognised as one pass, **because
   its rows do not share a timestamp.**

**THE DESK CANNOT COUNT ITS OWN COLLECTION PASSES IN EITHER DIRECTION.** *I have
been carrying this query on the open list for days as though it were work
waiting to be done. It was never runnable.*

### THE ANSWERABLE SUBSET, NAMED SO THE ITEM CLOSES CLEANLY RATHER THAN VANISHING

**`research_jobs.sources_ready_at` is one timestamp per job, set by
`markJobStage`.** *Job-driven collection passes ARE countable — one per job with
that column non-null.* **What stays uncountable is the 60-second source polling
and the 10/30-minute discovery re-looks**, which is most of the volume and all of
the cheap tier.

**A `pass_id` on `research_sources` would settle it.** That is a schema change in
`lib/market/store/` — **Ops's file, Ops's call, and I am not proposing it on the
strength of a query nobody has asked for since.**

### ONE FIGURE FROM THE RUN THAT SURVIVES ITS OWN DENOMINATOR

**43 of 323 `(ticker, trading_date)` pairs with at least one job — 13.3% — had NO
source row fetched that day at all.** *That does not depend on identifying
passes: zero rows is zero rows.* **One job in eight was asked about a name and
stored nothing new for it**, which is the fingerprint short-circuit doing exactly
what it exists to do, and the only part of the original question this snapshot
can answer.

**122. `trading_date` IS WRITER-ASSIGNED AND DEMONSTRABLY WRONG. "ZERO BARS FOR
09-04" WAS ASKED WITH IT, SO IT MAY BE THE SAME CLASS OF ERROR AS MY OWN `ACTIVE`
RETRACTION — A FLAW IN THE QUERY, NOT IN THE WORLD.**

### FIRST, THE CORRECTION I OWE: `repo.ts:163` — AND THE GUARDS ARE PASSED, NOT SKIPPED

*Integration corrected my "`repo.ts:163` is where to look", pointing out two
guards upstream: `runtime.ts:1426`'s `isTracked` filter and `repo.ts:160`'s
`bars.length === 0`. **Right that I sent a fixer downstream of both exits. Wrong
that line 163 may never have run**, and the chain says so.*

```ts
// runtime.ts:1209 — ONE handler, three lines apart
const events = this.engine.ingest(observation);   // fills runtime.minuteTrades
if (observation.bar) this.pendingBars.push(observation.bar);
```

1. **`activity_window` holds real counts ⇒ `minuteTrades` was populated ⇒ the
   observation carried a bar ⇒ `pendingBars` WAS pushed.** Same handler, no
   branch between them but `if (observation.bar)`.
2. **`activity` is computed by iterating `this.tickers`** (`recompute()`), and
   `isTracked` is `this.tickers.has(symbol)`. **A symbol with a written activity
   value was in the map, so the filter kept it.**
3. **`upsertTickerSessions` (`runtime.ts:1435`) runs LATER IN THE SAME `flush()`
   than the bar block (`:1421`).** 09-04's `ticker_session` rows exist, **so
   `flush()` ran to completion — and the bar block executed first.**

**BOTH GUARDS PASSED. THE INSERT RAN.** *So the search is not "did it run" but
"where did the rows go" — and item 120 already eliminated both deletion paths.*

### AND THE REMAINING EXIT IS THE LABEL, WHICH IS NOT DERIVED FROM THE DATA

```sql
PRIMARY KEY (symbol, ts)                      -- trading_date is NOT in the key
ON CONFLICT(symbol, ts) DO UPDATE SET ...     -- and DO UPDATE never sets it
```

**`trading_date` comes from `this.tradingDate` — the WRITER'S idea of the
session — never from `ts`.** *A stale or wrong `tradingDate` files a real bar
under the wrong day, and a query by `trading_date` then reports it missing.*

**THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. MEASURED ON `data/market.db`:**

```
rows whose trading_date != the ET date of their own ts:  19,915 of 1,340,336  (1.49%)
  2026-08-18 -> 2026-08-19    19,915
```

**Bars timestamped 09:23 ET on 08-19 are filed under `trading_date = 2026-08-18`.
The writer's session had not rolled.**

### SO THE 09-04 QUESTION HAS TO BE RE-ASKED

**"Zero bars for 09-04" was established with `WHERE trading_date = '2026-09-04'`.
That is the writer's label, not the bars' timestamps.** *The right question is
whether any bar's **`ts` falls on 09-04**, regardless of what it is labelled.*

**ONE QUERY, AND IT CAN DISSOLVE THE FINDING OR HARDEN IT:**

```sql
SELECT trading_date, COUNT(*), MIN(ts), MAX(ts)
  FROM minute_bars GROUP BY trading_date;
-- and the decisive one: bucket by the ET date of ts, not by trading_date.
```

**If 09-04's bars are sitting under another label, they were never missing.** *If
every row's label matches its own timestamp, the labelling hazard is excluded and
the write failure hardens — which is worth as much.*

**A CAUTION AGAINST MY OWN LEAD: the local mismatch runs FORWARD — new bars under
an OLD date. That direction would put 09-04's bars under 09-03, and 09-03 holds
1.06M, about ONE session rather than two.** *So the specific instance I measured
does not explain 09-04, and I am not claiming it does. **What it establishes is
that the mechanism exists and the query cannot see past it.***

### WHY THIS IS WORTH SAYING AT ALL

**It is the same shape as my own retraction four hours ago.** I concluded `ACTIVE`
was unreachable from a query against a current-state table, and the flaw was in
the comparison rather than in the world. **"Zero bars for 09-04" is a conclusion
drawn through a column that is assigned rather than derived, and nobody has
checked that column against the data it describes.**

*Item 114 is unaffected: every mismatch in the local store is `08-18 -> 08-19`,
and no 08-17 row is misfiled in either direction, so the session that measurement
walked is intact.*

**123. BOTH PATHS THAT FILL THE MINUTE-TRADE MAP ALSO PERSIST MINUTE BARS. SO
09-04 IS NOT "A WRITE THAT FAILED" — IT IS TWO INDEPENDENT WRITERS THAT BOTH
FAILED WHILE THEIR SHARED SIDE-EFFECT SUCCEEDED. AND THE ONE OPERATION KNOWN TO
HAVE TOUCHED THAT TABLE IS NOT ON THE ELIMINATED LIST.**

*Ops ran the `trading_date` query on production: **zero mislabelled rows across
2,116,296**, both groupings identical, the total leaving no room under any label
for a missing session. **My challenge failed and the write failure hardens.** It
was worth the slot because it could have dissolved the finding; it did not.*

### I WENT LOOKING FOR THE HOLE IN MY OWN ARGUMENT AND FOUND THE OPPOSITE

*My `activity.ts:259` inference — a populated map proves the feed delivered —
would break if some path filled `minuteTrades` **without** persisting bars. **A
startup reconstruction is exactly the shape that would do it**, so I checked.*

**THERE ARE EXACTLY TWO CALLERS OF `engine.ingest`:**

| | | persists? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runtime.ts:1209` | live handler | `pendingBars.push` → `:1426` filter → `upsertMinuteBars` |
| `runtime.ts:964` | startup backfill | **`upsertMinuteBars(this.db, this.tradingDate, normalized)` at `:975`, direct, bypassing the filter** |

**BOTH PERSIST.** *The backfill does not even go through the tracked-set gate —
it writes what it reconstructed.* **So my inference survives, and it is now
stronger than when I made it: every path that can populate `minuteTrades` also
writes `minute_bars`.**

### WHICH MAKES 09-04 SHARPER, NOT SOFTER

**`activity_window` on 09-04 holds real minute trade counts. Those can only come
from `minuteTrades`. Both writers of `minuteTrades` also write `minute_bars`. And
`minute_bars` holds nothing for that date.**

*So this is not one write path failing. **It is two independent writers — one
filtered and flush-driven, one direct and startup-driven — both failing to leave
a row, while the in-memory state they share arrived intact.*** **A single bug in
either call site cannot produce that.**

### ONE CHECK THAT SEPARATES THEM, ALREADY IN THE LOGS

`runtime.ts:999` logs on every startup:

```
[demand] startup backfill complete through <end> (<N> minute bars, <M> snapshots)
```

**`N` is `summary.minuteBarsIngested` — the exact count the backfill handed to
`upsertMinuteBars` at `:975`.** *On 09-04 that line says whether the direct
writer ran and what it thought it wrote.* **No query needed; it is already
written down.**

- **`N` large, table empty** ⇒ the write was attempted and did not land. **Points
  below the call sites, at the connection or the file.**
- **`N` zero or the line absent** ⇒ the backfill never ran, and only the live
  writer is in question.

### AND THE OPERATION THAT IS NOT ON THE ELIMINATED LIST

**Eliminated so far: prune, mode-wipe, lock, disk, schema, permissions,
`trading_date`, the tracked-set gate, the swallowed exception.**

**NOT ELIMINATED: THE 09-06 RESTORE ITSELF.** *It is the one operation known to
have written `minute_bars` deliberately, it produced **exactly** the two dates
that survive, and Ops found **fifteen `[demand] flush failed` on 09-06 and on no
other day**.*

**IF THE RESTORE REPLACED THE TABLE FROM A BACKUP TAKEN BEFORE 09-04, EVERY
OBSERVATION FITS WITHOUT ANY WRITE HAVING FAILED:** 09-02 and 09-03 present and
correctly labelled because they came from the backup; 09-04 absent because the
backup predates it; **09-04's `ticker_session` rows intact because the restore
touched a different table.**

**THIS IS A CANDIDATE, NOT A MECHANISM, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT.** *I
asserted a cause twice tonight and both were wrong.* **What settles it is what
the restore actually executed** — a table replace, or an insert of two dates
into a live table. **Ops ran it and knows; nobody has asked.**

**AND IT IS FALSIFIABLE IN ONE STEP:** if the restore inserted rows rather than
replacing the table, **and** the backfill log for 09-04 shows a large `N`, then

**124. `?? 0` IS NOT A CONFLATION TO BE FIXED — IT IS THE FILE'S CORE MECHANIC,
AND MAKING A MISSING SLOT UNKNOWN WOULD DESTROY DEATH DETECTION ENTIRELY. THE
LIVE ANSWER IS THE TRADE STREAM, WHICH ALREADY ARRIVES AND IS ALREADY IGNORED.**

*He asked: **"we're cutting off a whole minute because of a 'maybe'? how can we
make this element more live? this is valuable."** Integration proposed that the
settle margin papers over `?? 0` conflating "no bar arrived" with "zero trades",
and that a `null` slot would remove the need for it.*

### THAT CANDIDATE INVERTS THE MECHANIC THE FILE IS BUILT ON

`activity.ts:20`, and it is the file's own emphasis:

> ***"A DEAD MINUTE HAS NO BAR.** Alpaca emits no minute bar for a minute with no
> trades — measured, not assumed: BTCT on 2025-06-03 returns bars at 13:30, 13:32
> and 13:33 with `limit=3`, so 13:31 was not displaced by the limit, it does not
> exist. **Death therefore arrives as an ABSENT ROW rather than a low count.**"*

**ABSENCE IS THE DEATH SIGNAL.** *`?? 0` is not throwing information away — it is
reading the only signal the feed provides.* **If a missing slot became UNKNOWN,
every genuinely dead name would read UNKNOWN forever and the rule would detect
nothing.**

### THE REAL DISTINCTION IS NOT ABSENT-VS-PRESENT. IT IS HOW OLD THE SLOT IS.

**An absent slot from six minutes ago is dead. An absent slot from one minute ago
may be in flight. Nothing in the bar itself separates them — the discriminator is
ELAPSED TIME, and `settleMinutes` IS that discriminator.**

**So the margin is not a workaround for a defect. It is the mechanism doing
exactly the job the candidate wanted done**, and removing it removes the only
thing standing between "in flight" and "dead". *`activity.ts:156` withholding the
price window is a different case: there, withholding costs a line on a chart. Here
it would cost the verdict.*

**AND THE MARGIN CANNOT BE MADE FRACTIONAL.** The window is minute-grained, so
the smallest non-zero settle is one minute. **Measuring `received_at` is still
worth doing — it sizes the risk of `settleMinutes: 0` — but it cannot buy a
smaller margin, only the choice between one and none.**

### THE LIVE ANSWER IS ROUTE 2, AND IT IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS

**THE DESK ALREADY RECEIVES INDIVIDUAL TRADES.** `engine.ts:906` dispatches
`case 'trade'` to `ingestTrade` for every subscribed name.

**`ingestTrade` (`:1086`) COUNTS NOTHING.** It sets price, `priceAt`,
`priceSource`, session high/low and the after-hours extremes. **The messages
arrive, are parsed, are used for price, and are then discarded as an activity
signal** — the same shape as the sentence at the top of this file about trade
counts *"already parsed off every wildcard bar and until now scored on by
nothing."*

**A per-minute counter incremented in `ingestTrade` has NO SETTLE MARGIN AT ALL,
because a trade message IS the event. There is nothing in flight to wait for.**
The minute in progress becomes countable in real time.

**FOUR THINGS THAT ARE TRUE OF IT AND MUST TRAVEL WITH IT:**

1. **IT COVERS ONLY THE HIGH-RES SET — up to 250 names.** The wildcard BAR stream
   covers everything; trades cover only what is subscribed. **A trade-derived
   counter is live for board names and blank for the rest — a two-tier signal,
   and the tiers must be visibly different.**
2. **`ingestTrade` RETURNS EARLY THREE TIMES BEFORE IT DOES ANY WORK** —
   `price === null || price <= 0`, `!inSessionWindow`, and
   **`!isNewerObservation(runtime.priceAt, observation.ts)`**. *A counter placed
   after those guards would silently undercount every out-of-order print.* **It
   has to increment before the ordering guard, which means it is not a one-line
   change to an existing block.**
3. **IT IS NOT THE SAME NUMBER AS THE BAR COUNT.** Bars come from the consolidated
   tape with corrections; a live print stream includes trades that may later be
   cancelled or revised. **The live counter approximates and converges. The two
   series must never be rendered as one continuous line.**
4. **COST IS A MAP WRITE PER TRADE MESSAGE, NO NEW SUBSCRIPTION AND NO SECOND SIP
   CONNECTION.** *Cheap per message, and there are a great many messages in an
   active premarket.* **The map needs the same pruning `minuteTrades` has.**

### SO THE HONEST ANSWER TO HIM

**The "maybe" is real and the margin is the right response to it — for a
BAR-DERIVED count. It is not a workaround and it should not be shortened.**

**What makes the element live is not removing the wait. It is counting a source
that does not have one**, and the desk is already receiving that source and
already ignoring it for this purpose.

*Sizing, scope and whether it is worth the message-rate cost are Design's and
Ops's. **Nothing here is built and nothing should be until he has that.***

**125. THE MECHANISM WAS RIGHT AND THE QUANTITY WAS NEVER MEASURED. 200
MILLISECONDS, NOT A MINUTE — BUT THE GRAIN MEANS THE ONLY ALTERNATIVE IS ZERO,
AND TODAY'S SAMPLE DOES NOT BOUND THE TAIL THAT MATTERS.**

*Ops, on today's 20,498 bars: **live bars land 0.005s–0.200s after their minute
closes; the only later arrivals are 15 `updated-bar` corrections at ~30s.** Two
populations, no overlap.*

### WHAT I GOT WRONG, AND IT WAS THE NUMBER

I told him: ***"Absent at six minutes = dead. Absent at one minute = maybe in
flight."*** **The logic holds; the quantity was invented.** *Absence at one
SECOND already means dead on today's data.* **`settleMinutes: 1` spends 60
seconds to cover 0.2 — three hundred times the worst case that exists**, and
nobody had ever measured it.

*That is this desk's pattern in its cheapest form: **a parameter defended by the
soundness of the mechanism around it.** The comment at `activity.ts:89` explains
why a margin is needed and never says why it is one.*

### BUT THE MEASUREMENT DOES NOT UNLOCK A MIDDLE VALUE

**The window is minute-grained. `settleMinutes` is a count of SLOTS, so the
options are 1 (60s) or 0. There is no 1-second setting.** *So this does not tune
the margin down to fit the evidence — it changes the question to whether ZERO is
safe.*

### AND ON THAT, TWO THINGS PULL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS

**FOR ZERO — the harm is bounded by the rule itself.** `deadMinutes: 5` requires
**five consecutive** slots at or below the dead line. **A single late bar read as
zero cannot manufacture death; it would take five consecutive late minutes.**
*What one late slot CAN do is block a revival — `reviveMinutes: 2` needs two in a
row — so the realistic cost of zero is a delayed revival, not a false death.*
**That is a much smaller exposure than `activity.ts:89` implies, and the comment
does not mention the consecutiveness that protects it.**

**AGAINST ZERO — today's sample does not bound the tail that matters.**

1. **It is a PREMARKET sample.** The highest message rate of the day is 09:30,
   and `received_at` is stamped when the desk PROCESSES the message, not when the
   wire delivered it. **A busy event loop lengthens exactly this number, and
   premarket is when it is shortest.**
2. **It does not cover a reconnect or a stall.** *A dropped socket delivers a
   burst on resume, arbitrarily late.* **The desk spent tonight on a session
   where the feed's behaviour was anomalous; steady-state latency says nothing
   about that day.**
3. **15 corrections at 30s are a second population, and Ops is right that a dead
   minute never gets one** — a correction revises a bar that exists. *It does not
   bear on death detection. It does bear on the displayed COUNT being revised
   under the reader, which is a display question and Design's.*

### SO THE REVISED ANSWER, AND WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE

**CHANGED: I said the margin was the right size. I did not know its size, and it
is roughly 300x the observed need. Anyone reading my earlier answer as an
endorsement of `1` should not.**

**UNCHANGED — the refutation of the `null`-slot candidate.** *A dead minute has no
bar; absence is the death signal; `?? 0` reads the only signal the feed provides;
UNKNOWN slots would leave every dead name unknown forever.* **None of that
depends on the latency figure.**

**UNCHANGED — and now stronger — the trade-counter route.** *A count taken from
the trade stream has no margin question at all, at any latency, because the trade
IS the event.* **The latency measurement argues for it rather than against it.**

**THE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE `settleMinutes: 0`: the same `received_at`
distribution at the 09:30 open and across a reconnect, as a p99 and a max rather
than a range.** *Not premarket steady state. **The margin exists for the tail,
so the tail is the only part worth measuring.***

DIFFERENT CLOTHES — CONFIRMED IN MY FILE — AND THE WHY NOT BLOCK IS UNDER 5% OF

### THE COUPLING, VERIFIED RATHER THAN RELAYED

`engine.ts:1707`, inside `applyHighResSelection`:

```ts
const alive = (runtime: TickerRuntime): boolean => runtime.activity !== 'DEAD';
```

**CONFIRMED. THE HIGH-RES SET IS GATED ON THE `DEAD` VERDICT, SO ANY
TRADE-DERIVED SIGNAL INHERITS EVERY OPEN QUESTION ABOUT THAT VERDICT.** *It fails

gated by the thing under investigation, and Integration is right that nobody had

**AND THE COVERAGE IS ANTI-CORRELATED WITH THE TRADE.** The gate excludes names
judged quiet; **a name that wakes up is quiet-then-loud.** *The rows most likely

### OPTION (3), ONE NAME IN THE DRAWER — PRICED

**MEASURED, 2026-08-17, the 65 top-twelve entrants:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| busiest single name | **IPST — 1,308,065 trades**, 1,458/min average over 897 minutes |
| median entrant | **20,582 trades/session** ≈ 23/min |
| all 65 together | 6.53M trades/session |

**THE MAP DOES NOT GROW WITH TRADES. IT IS KEYED BY MINUTE SLOT**, so a session
holds at most ~900 entries per symbol whether the name trades 20,000 times or
1.3 million. *I told Integration this "needs the same pruning `minuteTrades`
has" — **`minuteTrades` has no pruning and needs none**, for exactly this

**⇒ THE COST OF (3) IS NOT CPU AND NOT MEMORY. IT IS ONE SUBSCRIPTION.** Opening
a drawer subscribes one symbol to trades; closing it unsubscribes. **At the

### THE `ingestTrade` SURGERY — SMALLER THAN I IMPLIED, AND THE SIZE IS A
### PLACEMENT DECISION RATHER THAN A VOLUME OF CODE

```ts
const price = observation.price ?? null;
if (price === null || price <= 0) return;                          // 1
if (!this.inSessionWindow(observation.ts)) return;                 // 2
if (!isNewerObservation(runtime.priceAt, observation.ts)) return;  // 3  <-- must count BEFORE
```

**The counter goes BETWEEN 2 AND 3, and that is the whole difficulty.**
- **After 1** — a null or non-positive price is a malformed print, not a trade.
- **After 2** — an out-of-session print must not land in a session minute.
- **BEFORE 3** — **an out-of-order print is a real trade in its own minute.**
  Counting after the ordering guard silently undercounts exactly the busy names.

**SIZE: two lines at the call site, one field on `TickerRuntime`, one
initialiser. No pruning.** *"Not a one-line change" was right about the reasoning
and overstated the code.*

### DOES IT MAKE `settleMinutes` MOOT? NO — CONFIRMED, AND THEY ARE TWO PIECES OF WORK

**A drawer-scoped live count never feeds `resolveActivity`.** The board's verdict
still comes from `minuteTrades`, which is bar-derived, which is what the margin
exists for. **The 1-vs-0 decision stays real, stays separate, and is unaffected
by (3).** *Sequence them independently.*

*The only version that WOULD make it moot is uniform live — option (1) — which
`stream.ts:288-290` rules out deliberately. **Flagging, not assuming**: that is a
bandwidth decision, not mine to reopen.*

### THE WHY NOT BUDGET — A BAND, WITH ITS ASSUMPTIONS NAMED

**THE DENOMINATOR, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE RATE. Dossiers, not jobs:**

```
2026-08-17  48      2026-08-20  89
2026-08-18  72      2026-08-21  59        mean ~65/day, range 48-89
2026-08-19  57                            325 versions over 231 tickers, 5 sessions
```

**THE MODEL MIX, VERIFIED NOT ASSUMED — read from `research_analysis_versions.model`:**

```
gpt-5.6-terra   299   (92%)
gpt-5.6-sol      26   ( 8%)
```

**This is the expensive half and it is where the block lands.** *The last two
estimates on this desk were 2.3x and 7.7x high for assuming a mix that was not
there; this one is read off the stored versions.*

**THE MARGINAL BLOCK.** Six fields, a closed six-rule list and four undetermined
reasons: **~400–800 added input tokens on every call** (schema + instructions),
**~80–200 output tokens** for the block itself.

```
terra  600 in x $2.00/M + 140 out x $12.00/M   = $0.0029 / dossier
sol    600 in x $4.00/M + 140 out x $20.00/M   = $0.0052 / dossier
at 92/8                                        = $0.0031 / dossier
x 65 dossiers/day                              ~ $0.20 / day

BAND:  $0.10/day  (48 dossiers, 400 in / 80 out)
       $0.35/day  (89 dossiers, 800 in / 200 out)
```

**AGAINST A ~$7–10 SESSION BASELINE: UNDER 5%, AND PLAUSIBLY UNDER 2%.**

**THREE THINGS THAT COULD MOVE IT, STATED:**
1. **REPAIRS ARE THE REAL RISK.** A repair re-sends the whole bundle. **A block
   the model fills badly multiplies the call, not the block** — and the repair
   path is where a new required field with a closed vocabulary would bite.
2. **CACHED INPUT CUTS IT.** The schema is byte-identical every call, so
   `cached_tokens` at $0.20/M terra could drop the input side ~10x. **Would push
   the band toward $0.10.**
3. **THE DOSSIER COUNT IS FROM AUGUST**, five sessions in the 08-23 snapshot.
   **Not verified against current volume.**

### AND THE COST THE NUMBER DOES NOT PRICE

***A block the model must fill for a name with nothing to say is where a taxonomy
starts inventing.***

**Twenty cents a day is not the decision.** The schema is
`additionalProperties: false` with **every key required**, so the block is
mandatory on **every dossier — including the majority with no catalyst at all**.
*A model asked six questions about a name with no event answers them anyway.*
**`validateCatalystEffect` degrades an unrecognised rule to UNDETERMINED rather
than discarding it, which is the right design and also means the invented answer
is RECORDED rather than refused.** *That is the cost, and it does not appear in a
token count.*

**127. THE SENTINEL ALREADY EXISTS, THE DECLINED/UNRECOGNISED SPLIT IS ALREADY
IMPLEMENTED, AND "THE MAJORITY HAVE NO CATALYST" WAS MINE AND WRONG — IT IS 29%.**

*Integration refused to accept "the schema requires it" as a constraint of
nature. Right to refuse: the schema is ours. But the thing it proposed adding is
already there.*

### 1. THE "NO CATALYST" SENTINEL IS ALREADY THE CANONICAL EMPTY VALUE

`effect.ts:53` — `Side` includes **`'NONE'`**. `validateAxis`:

```ts
// `NONE` is the one side that needs no basis: nothing was claimed.
if (typed === 'NONE') return { side: 'NONE', basis: null };
```

**`NONE` / `NONE` with null bases, `priceCapped: null`, `timeToEffect: 'UNKNOWN'`
IS "there is no catalyst effect here"** — no basis, no source ids, no reasoning
demanded. *It is exactly the default fixture in `whyNot.test.ts`.*

**SO THE BLOCK IS REQUIRED AND ITS CONTENT IS NOT.** *I wrote "a model asked six
questions about a name with no event answers them anyway." **The schema gives it
a one-word way to decline on both axes, and I turned a schema constraint into an
inevitability.***

### 2. AND THE POPULATION IS SMALLER THAN I SAID — MEASURED, 325 STORED VERSIONS

```
catalystStatus     FRESH_FOUND       138  42%
                   SECONDARY_STALE    91  28%
                   UNKNOWN            78  24%
                   NONE_FOUND         17   5%
                   CONFLICTING         1   0%
```

**NO USABLE CATALYST = `UNKNOWN` + `NONE_FOUND` = 29%. NOT "the majority", WHICH
IS WHAT I TOLD INTEGRATION.** *70% carry a real catalyst, and for those the six
questions are legitimate rather than invented.*

**⇒ THE INVENTION RISK IS CONFINED TO ABOUT A THIRD OF THE CORPUS — and it is
precisely the third where an honest answer already exists and costs nothing.**

### 3. THE COST BARELY MOVES, WHICH CONFIRMS COST WAS NEVER THE QUESTION

Empty form ≈ **25–30 output tokens** against ≈140 populated. Blended at 29/71 ≈
**108 vs 140** → **~$0.18/day instead of ~$0.20.**

**A SENTINEL DOES NOT DISSOLVE THIS DECISION. It was never a money decision.**

### 4. DECLINED vs UNRECOGNISED: ALREADY DISTINGUISHED, AND ROUTED DIFFERENTLY

*Integration was right that these must not collapse — it is the night's lesson
arriving in a new field. **It has not collapsed.***

- **`NONE`** → `basis: null`. A deliberate "nothing claimed".
- **Unrecognised** → `UNDETERMINED` with a **named reason**:
  `UNRECOGNISED_RULE`, `RULE_DIRECTION_MISMATCH`, `CONTENT_NOT_IN_EVIDENCE`,
  `NOT_SEARCHED`.

**And `whyNot()` routes them to DIFFERENT VERDICTS:** `NONE` with coverage gives
`NO_OBJECTION_FOUND`; **any UNDETERMINED axis forces `NOTHING_COLLECTED`**, even
with a healthy source count. *The distinction is not merely recorded — it changes
what the report says.*

### THE RESIDUAL RISK, AND IT IS A PROMPT PROPERTY RATHER THAN A SCHEMA ONE

**`NONE` BEING AVAILABLE IS NOT `NONE` BEING USED.** *Whether the model declines
honestly on the 29% is a property of the instructions, and it is measurable —
run the arm in replay and count how often it returns `NONE`/`NONE` on names whose
catalyst status is `UNKNOWN` or `NONE_FOUND`.*

**AND THAT MEASUREMENT IS EXACTLY THE TWO DEMOTED ONES (item 111), WHICH CANNOT
RUN BECAUSE NOTHING PRODUCES A `CatalystEffect`.** **The thing that would de-risk
the build requires the build.** *That circularity is the real sequencing
constraint, and it is not resolved by anything in this item — but a replay arm
breaks it without a deploy, which is the cheapest way through.*

**SO THE ANSWER TO "IS IT GENUINELY FORCED" IS NO — AND THE DECISION IS SMALLER
AND CLEANER THAN I HANDED IT OVER:** not *"is a mandatory block worth $0.20/day"*
but ***"will the model say NONE when there is nothing, and are we willing to run
one replay arm to find out before shipping it."***

**128. "GOES SILENT" MEANS 30 TRADES A MINUTE, NOT 300. THE TRADE-COUNT-VERSUS-
VOLUME DIVERGENCE IS REAL, IS 70% CLOSING AUCTION, AND IS 0.03% OF MINUTES IN
HIS WINDOW. AND THE PROVENANCE IS NAMED IN THE FILE BUT NOT CARRIED BY IT.**

### 1. THE THRESHOLDS, THEIR UNITS, AND THE DERIVATION

```
activeTradesPerMinute  300     TRADES per minute -- a count of prints, not shares
deadRatio               10     the dead line is DERIVED: 300 / 10 = 30 trades/min
```

**Neither is separately configurable, deliberately.** `activity.ts:44`:

> *"The dead line is DERIVED as `active / deadRatio`, never configured
> separately, because the 10x is the trader's and a second number could drift
> away from the ratio he actually chose."*

**And `DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_CONFIG` is a hardcoded constant with no environment
override anywhere** — `resolveActivity` accepts a `config` parameter and nothing
in production passes one.

### 2. WHICH LINE DOES WHAT — AND "SILENT" WAS THE WRONG WORD

| verdict | rule |
| --- | --- |
| **DEAD** | **5 consecutive** minutes **at or below 30** trades/min |
| **ACTIVE** | **2 consecutive** minutes **at or above 300** trades/min |
| between 30 and 300 | **NEITHER. The previous state persists.** |

`activity.ts:325`:

> *"The band between the dead line and the active line is neither: it neither
> confirms death nor earns a return, so the previous state persists. That is
> what the trader's 10x ratio buys — **it is a hysteresis band rather than two
> unrelated numbers**, which is also why the dead line is derived from it."*

**⇒ "GOES SILENT" MEANS FELL TO 30 OR BELOW, NOT 300.** *A name doing 200
trades a minute is not silent, is not dead, and does not lose its badge.*

### 3. TRADE COUNT OVER SHARE VOLUME — DELIBERATE, AND THE EVIDENCE IS NOT IN THIS REPO

`activity.ts:15`, verbatim:

> *"The measure is minute TRADE COUNT — **the one the viscosity research
> confirmed as meaningful**, already parsed off every wildcard bar and already
> persisted, and until now scored on by nothing."*

**SO THE CHOICE IS RECORDED AS DELIBERATE AND ATTRIBUTED TO A PRIOR STUDY. THE
STUDY IS NOT HERE.** It lives at `A:\trade_research\momentum\viscosity`, named
only in `docs/DATA-ARCHIVE.md:205`. **A reader of `activity.ts` is told the
conclusion and cannot check it.**

*That is stronger than folklore — a real programme is named — and weaker than a
citation. **He is entitled to know which it is before defending the number.***

### 4. NOTHING ELSE USES SHARE VOLUME FOR LIVENESS

`minuteVolumes` **is** collected and **is** used — after-hours volume sums, the
cumulative volume base, VWAP accumulation (`engine.ts:739/761/816/945/951`).
**Never for liveness. `trade_count` is the only liveness input anywhere on the
desk.**

**129. `settleMinutes: 1` MARKS A RECOVERING NAME DEAD, AND HYSTERESIS THEN HOLDS
IT THERE. NOT A PRODUCT DECISION — A DEFECT, AND IT BITES THE WAKE-UP TRANSITION
HE TRADES.**

*Integration asked what actually differs between 1 and 0 under hysteresis, and to
name situations rather than rules. **Run, not reasoned** — six cases through the
real `resolveActivity` at both settings.*

```
A. busy name, newest minute ABSENT, acquiring from UNKNOWN   (the reverting test)
     settle=1 -> ACTIVE   [900,900,900,900,900]
     settle=0 -> UNKNOWN  [900,900,900,900,0]

B. busy name, newest minute ABSENT, already ACTIVE
     settle=1 -> ACTIVE   settle=0 -> ACTIVE      <- no difference

C. four quiet minutes, busy t-1 that has NOT arrived
     settle=1 -> DEAD     settle=0 -> DEAD        <- no difference

D. four quiet minutes, busy t-1 that DID arrive
     settle=1 -> DEAD     [5,5,5,5,5]
     settle=0 -> ACTIVE   [5,5,5,5,900]           <- OPPOSITE VERDICTS

E. genuinely dead across the span
     settle=1 -> DEAD     settle=0 -> DEAD        <- no difference

F. revival, two busy minutes at the end, previous DEAD
     settle=1 -> ACTIVE   settle=0 -> ACTIVE      <- no difference
```

### 1. WHAT ACTUALLY DIFFERS — AND IT IS NOT "EVERY TRANSITION A MINUTE EARLIER"

**Four of the six cases are IDENTICAL.** Steady state, genuine death, revival and
the missing-bar case all agree. **The margin does nothing in the situations it
was written for.**

**THE TWO THAT DIFFER:**

- **A — first acquisition.** From `UNKNOWN`, settle=1 earns ACTIVE a minute
  sooner. *It "wins" only because it is judging older data that happens to be
  complete.*
- **D — AND THIS IS THE FINDING. A name quiet for four minutes whose fifth
  minute is busy, with that bar ARRIVED: settle=1 returns DEAD. settle=0 returns
  ACTIVE.** *Not a minute apart. **Opposite**, at the same instant, and the
  stale one is wrong.*

**AND UNDER HYSTERESIS THAT WRONG DEAD IS STICKY.** Once DEAD, revival needs
**two consecutive minutes at or above 300**. A name trading in the 30–300 band
after waking up **never earns it back** and sits falsely DEAD indefinitely.

**⇒ THE PARAMETER COSTS A WRONG VERDICT ON EXACTLY THE QUIET-THEN-LOUD
TRANSITION HE TRADES**, and everything downstream reads it: the subscription
selector drops the name, `queue.ts:83` declines research on it, the badge says
dead.

### 2. WHAT THE REVERTING TEST RETURNS AT 0 — `UNKNOWN`, NOT `DEAD`

**Integration's suspicion is confirmed: it does not manufacture death.** The
busy slots keep the dead run from completing; the zero merely stops ACTIVE being
*earned*, so the previous state persists — `UNKNOWN` in the fixture.

**The test guards ONE MINUTE OF DELAY IN FIRST ACQUISITION. Nothing more.**

### 3. IS THE ASSERTION STILL WANTED? NO — AND THE TRADE RUNS THE WRONG WAY

Its docstring defends against *"manufacture death every minute on every name"*.
**Case C is that scenario and both settings agree — it cannot happen.** What the
test actually buys is case A: acquiring a badge sixty seconds sooner **on a name
whose most recent minute nobody has looked at.**

**Against that, case D gives a WRONG DEAD on a recovering name, and hysteresis
makes it stick.**

> **SO THIS IS NOT A PRODUCT DECISION AND SHOULD NOT GO TO HIM AS ONE.** A
> parameter costing a minute of freshness, defended by a comment that is false
> and a test guarding an impossibility, **whose only measurable behavioural
> effect is to mislabel the transition the desk exists to catch.**

### WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING

**Case D needs the wake-up minute's bar to have arrived before the evaluation** —
0.005–0.200s premarket, ≤0.673s all day, so it usually has. **I have not measured
how often the four-quiet-then-loud pattern occurs**, only that when it does the
two settings disagree and 1 is wrong.

*And case A is a real if small loss: a name acquiring ACTIVE from UNKNOWN takes
one minute longer at 0. **That is the honest cost of the change** and it is worth
naming beside the benefit rather than after it.*

**The change is one constant plus nine test expectations, five of which are
Design's. Case D belongs in `activity.test.ts` whichever way it goes** — nothing
currently asserts it, which is why the parameter survived.

**130. CASE G EXISTS. A FEED STALL MARKS THE ENTIRE BOARD DEAD AT ONCE, NEITHER
SETTING PROTECTS AGAINST IT, AND IT WEAKENS AN INFERENCE I MADE IN ITEM 117.**

*Integration asked whether a delivery gap long enough to empty the window
produces death at both settings — "the actual scenario the original comment
feared, arriving through a door the parameter never covered." **Run, not
reasoned.***

```
G.  FEED STALL   busy name @1,500/min, map populated from 10-20 min ago,
                 nothing in the judged window
                 settle=1 -> DEAD   [0,0,0,0,0]  map size 11
                 settle=0 -> DEAD   [0,0,0,0,0]  map size 11

G2. RESTART      map entirely empty
                 settle=1 -> UNKNOWN            settle=0 -> UNKNOWN

G3. SHORT GAP    busy through t-7, nothing after
                 settle=1 -> DEAD   settle=0 -> DEAD   map size 4
```

### THE DESK IS PROTECTED AGAINST A RESTART AND UNPROTECTED AGAINST A STALL

**`activity.ts:259` guards `minuteTrades.size === 0` → UNKNOWN**, and its comment
says why: *"after a restart the maps are empty, and empty must never read as
silent."*

**A STALL DOES NOT EMPTY THE MAP. IT LEAVES IT POPULATED FROM BEFORE THE STALL**,
so the window fills with `?? 0` and the name reads DEAD. **A name trading 1,500
times a minute goes DEAD because the feed stopped, not because it did.**

**AND G3 SHOWS HOW LITTLE IT TAKES: a gap of about six or seven minutes is
enough.** *Every name simultaneously, and under hysteresis each then needs two
consecutive minutes at or above 300 to recover.*

> **THIS IS THE SCENARIO THE ORIGINAL COMMENT FEARED — "manufacture death every
> minute, on every name" — ARRIVING THROUGH A DOOR `settleMinutes` NEVER
> COVERED.** *The margin insures a sub-second delivery delay. It does nothing
> about a six-minute one, at either value.*

**SEPARATE FROM THE 1-VS-0 CHANGE AND IT MUST NOT RIDE IT.** Case D is a wrong
verdict at one setting; **case G is a wrong verdict at both**, and fixing it
means telling a stall from silence — which the store cannot currently do,
because a missing bar is the death signal.

### AND IT WEAKENS MY OWN ITEM 117

I wrote: ***"`DEAD 7,757` MEANS 7,757 SYMBOLS HAD A NON-EMPTY `minuteTrades` MAP
IN MEMORY ⇒ bars were arriving ⇒ 09-04 was a WRITE failure, not a FEED
failure."***

**CASE G BREAKS THE MIDDLE STEP.** A stalled feed leaves a populated map and
still yields DEAD. **So `DEAD` proves the map was non-empty AT SOME POINT IN THE
SESSION — not that bars were arriving at the moment of evaluation.**

**INTEGRATION'S EVIDENCE WAS THE RIGHT ONE AND THIS IS WHY.** Its proof was the
**values**: `activity_window` holding `[160,184,257,365,14]` — *real counts, on a
date that persisted no bars.* **A stall would have written `[0,0,0,0,0]`. Values
prove delivery; the DEAD verdict does not.** *It said its proof was stronger than
mine and did not know this was the reason; it is.*

**THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES ON ITS EVIDENCE, NOT ON MINE.** 09-04 was still
receiving and not storing — **2,369 of 7,757 windows carry real counts, which no
stall produces.**

### WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY

**No stall has been observed.** Ops measured 920,000 bars across a full session
with **no gap and no reconnect**, and flagged that itself: *observed-absent is
weaker than cannot-occur.* **Case G is a latent failure demonstrated in the
rule, not an incident.** *It becomes urgent the first time the feed drops for
six minutes during a session, and nothing today would distinguish that from the
whole board going quiet.*

**131. RETRACTING "CANNOT". BOTH DISCRIMINATORS ARE LIVE — ONE IS A FIELD THAT
ALREADY EXISTS ON THE WRONG SIDE OF ONE BOUNDARY.**

*I wrote that fixing case G "means telling a stall from silence, which the store
cannot currently do, because a missing bar IS the death signal." **Integration
refused to record `cannot` on two unchecked candidates. Right to refuse — both
are live.***

### DISCRIMINATOR 1: `lastBarAt` EXISTS, IS SERVED, AND THE VERDICT CANNOT SEE IT

**`worker/runtime.ts:1221` — `this.health.lastBarAt = now`, set on every `bar`
and `updatedBar` observation, DESK-WIDE.** It reaches `types.ts:515`,
`readModel.ts:108` and `diagnostics.ts:340`, and Design read it off the 04:00
payload as *"feed streaming, `lastBarAt` 12s old."*

**IT LIVES ON THE WORKER'S `health`. `resolveActivity` is called from
`engine.ts:1142` inside `refreshDerived`, and the engine holds no reference to
it.**

> **THE FIELD IS NOT MISSING. IT IS ON THE WRONG SIDE OF ONE BOUNDARY, and the
> worker owns both sides.**

**AND IT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE FOR THE JOB: it answers "when did ANY bar last
arrive."** *A six-minute-old `lastBarAt` is a stalled feed. It cannot be confused
with a quiet market, because in a real market some name always prints.*

### DISCRIMINATOR 2: THE POPULATION, AND THE ENGINE ALREADY VISITS EVERY NAME

`recompute()` loops `this.tickers` and calls `refreshDerived` per runtime, **so
the count of names with a non-empty window is available in the pass that is
already happening.**

**ONE ORDERING PROBLEM, AND IT IS NOT FATAL:** the verdict for the first name is
computed before the count exists. **Two options, both cheap** — `recompute()`
already runs more than one loop over `this.tickers`, so a counting pass costs a
second iteration; or carry the previous cycle's count, **which is one cycle stale
against a stall that lasts six minutes and spans many.**

**Integration's framing is the argument: a market in which every name stops in
the same minute does not happen. 09-04 is the proof — 2,369 windows with real
counts against 5,388 zero. THAT DISTRIBUTION IS A MARKET. ALL-ZERO IS A STALL.**

### SO `CANNOT` WAS WRONG AND IT WAS THE DANGEROUS KIND OF WRONG

*It is the word that stops the next reader looking, which is the same mechanism
as the false comment that protected `settleMinutes` for three months.* **I wrote
it about a field that is already computed, already served, and already on
screen.**

### THE LIMIT WORTH NAMING BEFORE ANYONE BUILDS EITHER

**A MARKET-WIDE HALT LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE A STALL TO BOTH.** During a LULD
market-wide circuit breaker no bars arrive, `lastBarAt` ages, and every window
empties. **Whatever is built must decide what it does then** — *"the feed is
fine and nothing is trading" is a third state, and neither discriminator
distinguishes it from a stall.*

*Marking every name DEAD during a halt is arguably as wrong as doing it during a
stall, and the desk already tracks halt state per symbol (`halt_state`,
`HALT`/`RESUME` events), so the input for that exists too.* **Not scoped, named.**

**NO DESIGN PROPOSED AND NONE ASKED FOR. The finding is that `cannot` is
unearned and there are two candidates, one of which is a single value crossing a
single boundary.**

**132. THE MODEL ALREADY DECLINES 96% OF THE TIME WHEN IT HAS NOTHING. THE
INVENTION RISK IS SMALLER THAN EITHER OF US FRAMED IT, AND THE EVIDENCE WAS
ALREADY STORED.**

*Before recommending the `omitSheetPrior` control, asked the cheaper question:
**what does the model already do on the no-catalyst population, in the required
fields it already fills?** 325 stored versions, 95 with `catalystStatus` of
`UNKNOWN` or `NONE_FOUND`.*

```
catalystGrade            UNKNOWN 76 · NONE 15 · MODERATE_MIXED_SECONDARY 4
plausiblyExplainsMove    null 74 · false 18 · true 3
confidence               LOW 76 · MEDIUM 17 · HIGH 2
unknowns[] populated     95 of 95   (100%)
```

**91 OF 95 DECLINE A GRADE. IT CLAIMS THE MOVE IS EXPLAINED THREE TIMES IN
NINETY-FIVE. IT NAMES WHAT IT DOES NOT KNOW EVERY SINGLE TIME.**

### AND `plausiblyExplainsMove` IS THE EXISTING ANALOGUE OF THE EFFECT BLOCK

*A required judgement field with an honest opt-out — and **the model takes the
opt-out 74 times in 95**.* **That is the closest thing the schema already has to
`NONE`/`NONE`, on the same population, from the same model under the same prompt
discipline.**

**⇒ THE DESIGN LESSON RATHER THAN THE BUDGET ONE: give the effect block an
opt-out as visible as `plausiblyExplainsMove: null` and it will be used.** *The
risk was never that the schema forced invention — item 127 already killed that —
it is that a block written without a prominent decline would invite it.*

### SO I AM RECOMMENDING AGAINST RUNNING `omitSheetPrior` FIRST

**It is a proxy for a proxy.** It measures how much the prior moves the fields
that exist **today**; the effect block does not exist, so it cannot measure the
prior's influence on it. **It would spend money to reduce uncertainty about a
number the stored dossiers have largely answered.**

*It stays worth running for its own sake — the automatic grade not being
independent of the prior is a real question — **but it is not a gate on this
build and I was wrong to sequence it as one.***

### AND A LABELLING CONFLICT THAT WOULD CHANGE WHAT THE CONTROL MEASURES

`bundle.ts:94` types the prior as **`label: 'HUMAN_REVIEWED_PRIOR_ANALYSIS'`** —
catalyst, grade, structure, cycle, warnings, float quality, notes.

`config.ts:63` describes the same thing as ***"another model's conclusion"***.

**ONE OF THOSE IS WRONG.** *If the Sheet is his own written analysis, the control
measures how much the desk's automatic grade is anchored to HIS judgement. If it
is another model's output, it measures machine-to-machine contamination.*
**Those are different findings and the same flag would produce both.** Worth
settling before anyone runs it, and not settleable from this repo.

**133. HE REVIEWS NOTHING, AND 46% OF ALL ESCALATIONS TO THE EXPENSIVE MODEL
FIRE ON DISAGREEING WITH "HUMAN REVIEW". THE DESK ONLY READS THAT SHEET AND
NOBODY IN THIS REPO KNOWS WHAT WRITES IT.**

*He corrected my item 132 framing: **"I don't review ANYTHING."** So the block
labelled `HUMAN_REVIEWED_PRIOR_ANALYSIS` is not human-reviewed, and the question
becomes what it actually is.*

### THE DESK NEVER WRITES THE SHEET — SO IT IS NOT ITS OWN OUTPUT LOOPING BACK

`googleSheets.ts:22` — scopes are **`spreadsheets.readonly`** and
`drive.metadata.readonly`. `sheetPrior.ts:9` — *"Read-only is enforced by

**⇒ NOT A FEEDBACK LOOP FROM THE DESK. The Sheet is populated by something
OUTSIDE this repo, and the repo cannot say what.**

### AND THE PREMISE IS LOad-BEARING, NOT DECORATIVE

`escalation.ts:170` escalates to **`sol` — the expensive tier** — on a material
Sheet-vs-automatic disagreement, and the recorded reason reads verbatim:

> **`"${dispute.field}: human review says ${dispute.sheet}, automatic analysis

**MEASURED, 325 stored versions, escalation reasons from `metadata`:**

SHEET_AUTO_CONFLICT                12    <- 46% of all escalations
SUPPLY_RECONCILIATION_INCONSISTENT   7
COMPETING_SUPPLY_INSTRUMENTS         5
ELIGIBILITY_CONTRADICTION            2
                                    26   = exactly the 26 sol versions

**THE LARGEST SINGLE DRIVER OF EXPENSIVE-TIER SPEND IS DISAGREEMENT WITH A

### WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SAY

**IT DOES NOT SAY THE ESCALATIONS WERE WRONG.** *Disagreement with an
independent source may genuinely warrant a second opinion — that is a defensible
design.* **What is not defensible is that nobody chose it**: the criterion was
built on *"evidence that a human disagreed"* (`sheetPrior.ts:5` — *"the worker
had no way to know a human had disagreed"*), and that is false.

**AND IT CONTAMINATES ITEM 132.** The 96%-decline base rate I measured yesterday
came from dossiers produced **with** this prior in the bundle. *If the Sheet
carries another model's conclusion, the decline may be INHERITED rather than
independent* — **which is exactly what `omitSheetPrior` would separate, and is
the strongest argument yet for running it.** *I recommended against it hours ago
on the assumption the prior was his own judgement. That assumption is dead.*

### THE ONE QUESTION THE REPO CANNOT ANSWER

**WHAT WRITES THAT SHEET?** *A previous tool, an older model, a one-off
historical fill, or a process nobody here has seen.* **Until that is known:**

- the escalation reason string is false and should not say "human review";
- **46% of expensive-tier spend rests on an unknown source's opinion**;
- and every "automatic" grade in the corpus was formed with that opinion in the
  bundle.

*He supplied what the repo could not: **the Sheet is written by the After-Hours

**144. HE CONFIRMED FIRST PRINT WITH THE TRADE COUNT — AND ONE RULE UN-COLLAPSES
AFTER-HOURS, WHICH CONTRADICTS ITEM 143.**

*My VWAP recommendation was wrong and he caught it in four words: **"why would
you do vwap?"** **A VWAP is an average over a window; an open is a point.** A name
that moves 10% inside its first minute has a VWAP in the middle of that, so "move
since the open" would read ~5% before anything happened — a bias of half the
first minute's range, built into the origin.*

**AND IT DOES NOT EVEN SOLVE WHAT I INVOKED IT FOR.** *With one odd-lot print the
volume-weighted average of one print IS that print.* **The robustness only
appears when there are many prints, and with many prints the plain open was
already fine. It fails exactly in the case it was for.** *I reached for a
robustness technique without checking it preserved the quantity's meaning.*

### THE RULE HE CONFIRMED

> **Session open = the FIRST PRINT of that session. One rule, all three sessions.
> The anchoring minute's TRADE COUNT travels with it, so a thin anchor is legible
> rather than smoothed away.**

*The desk's own pattern rather than a substitute number — the same shape as
`coverage: 'PARTIAL'` on the session VWAPs and `floatConfidence: 'UNKNOWN'` on
the structure block.* **A minute bar's `open` IS the first print of that minute,
so the first bar of the session supplies it directly.**

### AND THE CONSEQUENCE I OWE INTEGRATION: ITEM 143'S COLLAPSE IS WRONG NOW

**Item 143 said after-hours collapses to one figure because "its session open IS
today's 16:00 close, which IS its relevant last."** *That held while the session
open was DEFINED as the prior close. Under a uniform first-print rule it does
not:*

```
AH relevant last  = today's RTH close     (the closing print, 16:00)
AH session open   = the FIRST AH PRINT    (a different print, after 16:00)
```

**THEY ARE TWO DIFFERENT PRINTS, SO AFTER-HOURS GETS TWO DISTINCT FIGURES LIKE
THE OTHER SESSIONS** — and the difference between them is itself the after-hours
gap. *Which is the same decomposition as premarket: gapped in, then moved.*

**⇒ MORE CONSISTENT THAN WHAT I TOLD INTEGRATION, AND I TOLD INTEGRATION THE
OPPOSITE.** *The collapse was an artefact of my definition, not a property of the
session, and the one-rule answer removes it.*

### SCOPE, NOT BUILT — AND TWO TRAPS

1. **"FIRST" MUST MEAN EARLIEST TIMESTAMP, NOT FIRST RECEIVED.** *Bars arrive out
   of order — `isNewerObservation` guards exist across the engine for exactly
   that.* **A naive `if (open === null) open = bar.open` anchors on whichever bar
   the socket delivered first**, so a 04:01 bar ahead of the 04:00 bar would
   silently become the open.
2. **A CORRECTED BAR MUST MOVE THE ANCHOR.** `updatedBar` revises a minute, and
   `ingestBar` already threads `previous` for volume; the open needs the same
   treatment or a revised first minute leaves a stale origin.

**Where it goes: beside `accumulateVwap`, which already classifies every bar with
`vwapSessionForTs(bar.ts, this.tradingDate, this.rthCloseMinutes)`** — live,
tested, and already handling an early close. **Not a minute-bar query, and not a
third implementation of the session boundary.**

**HELD until after tonight's deploy.** *The supply bound ships tonight as its own
named change; a second one in the same window is the attribution failure I have
been holding everyone else to.*

### 3. THE JUDGEMENT, AND IT IS NOT FACT-VERSUS-PROXY

**A prior high IS a fact. Carrying it does not make the desk a signal product.**

> **BUT RENDERING IT AS A DISTANCE FROM LIVE PRICE DOES — because that
> subtraction has exactly one use.**

*"Prior high 4.80" is an observation. **"Price 4.79 · prior high 4.80" on one row
is a trigger, rendered as two facts with the reader doing the arithmetic.**
Nobody has to label anything; proximity does it.*

**AND THE SHAPE IS ALREADY ON HIS BOARD: `AH VWAP +$0.027 / +1.0%` is a level
expressed as a distance from price.** *So the question is not hypothetical — it
has a shipped precedent.*

**THE PRECEDENT DOES NOT LICENSE IT, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS REAL. A VWAP IS AN
AVERAGE — where trading has been, which is context. A HIGH IS A LEVEL SOMEONE
DEFENDS** — where stops and resting orders cluster, **which is precisely why
"over the high" is a strategy and "over VWAP" is not.** *An extreme is actionable
in a way a mean is not.*

**AND THE DESK IS CLOSER THAN IT LOOKS: `NEW_HOD` ALREADY FIRES.** *So "has it
taken out the high" is already computed. Add a prior-session high and render
proximity, and the board is one join from "1c from the level, and it just broke a
prior high" — a trigger with no label on it and nobody having decided to build
one.*

### SO THE RECOMMENDATION SPLITS THE AUTHORISED HALF IN TWO

**CONTINUITY IS SAFE AND IS THE BETTER HALF.** *`priorCycles` and
`formerRunnerStatus` cannot be turned into an entry — a familiar face is context
with no threshold in it. It is also already computed and currently unrendered.*

**LEVELS ARE SAFE AS LEVELS AND NOT AS DISTANCES.** **Carry a number with its
window named; refuse the gap-to-price rendering.**

**AND THE HONEST LIMIT: THAT IS A RENDERING CONSTRAINT AND RENDERING IS NOT
MINE.** *I cannot enforce it from the compute — a surface can subtract two
fields I publish.* **So if the desk wants the guarantee it has to be a stated
rule on the surface, not a property of the data, and someone other than me has
to hold it.**

**146. THE ACVA GAP IS ANCHORED CORRECTLY. BUT THE ROW CARRIES A SECOND READING
INTEGRATION ASKED ME TO LOOK FOR, AND ITS DISCRIMINATOR IS ALREADY STORED.**

*He said `PM GAP +43.4%` is "not accurate — it's up 43% INCLUDING AH." Integration
read it as right-number-wrong-label and asked me to check the compute rather than
assume it.*

### THE ANCHOR IS THE PRIOR RTH CLOSE, AND THAT IS CORRECT

`derive.ts:24` `resolveReferenceRthClose`:

```
rthHasClosed && usable(today)  ->  CURRENT_SESSION   (today's 16:00 close)
usable(prior)                  ->  PRIOR_SESSION     (yesterday's 16:00 close)
otherwise                      ->  null
```

**In premarket `rthHasClosed` is false, so it resolves to `PRIOR_SESSION`** and
`percentChange` is measured from **yesterday's official close**. *An after-hours
move from yesterday evening is inside that number by construction — the price now
reflects everything since 16:00 and the anchor predates it.* **Integration's
reading holds: the number is right, the word `PM` is wrong, and the fix is a
label.**

### BUT `PM VWAP +$0.000 / +0.0%` HAS TWO READINGS AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME ROW

**Integration asked for a reading where something IS wrong that also produces all
three numbers. There is one.**

| | what happened | `+$0.000` is | `RVOL 0.0x` is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **(a)** | **no premarket prints at all** | **a NULL rendered as a measurement** | true |
| **(b)** | **one or two premarket prints** | true — VWAP equals the only print, which is the price | true, rounds from a tiny number |

**Under (a) the desk computes `vwap: null, volume: null, coverage: 'UNAVAILABLE'`
(`engine.ts:1149`) and a surface showing `+$0.000` has turned an absence into a
zero** — *this desk's oldest failure, on his live board, in the row he was
already looking at.*

**THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ALREADY STORED AND IT IS ONE COLUMN.**
**`pm_vwap_coverage`** — `UNAVAILABLE` means (a) and the delta is fabricated;
`PARTIAL`/`COMPLETE` with `pm_vwap_volume > 0` means (b) and every number on the
row is honest. *`pm_vwap_volume` is the same check from the other side.*

**I cannot query production, so I am naming the test rather than the answer.**

### AND IT IS THE EXACT FAILURE THE MOVE FAMILY MUST NOT REPEAT

*Integration asked what `Move` does with a row that has no premarket prints.*
**Nothing, correctly: no first print means `sessionOpenPrice.premarket` stays
null, so `price: null` and `move: null`.** *It cannot render 0% because it has no
origin to divide by.*

> **BUT THAT IS ONLY HALF THE GUARANTEE.** *`sessionOpens` being optional and its
> fields nullable stops the COMPUTE from inventing a zero. It does not stop a
> surface rendering `null` as `+0.0%` — which is what reading (a) would mean is
> already happening one column to the left.*

**So if (a) is true it is not only a live defect, it is a demonstration of the
failure mode the Move family is walking into, on the same row, before Move has
shipped.** *That is worth more than the label fix.*
